/**
 * Issue #826 — integration test for the cleanup script's main() end-to-end.
 *
 * Background: PR #813 Phase 2 shipped 16 unit tests for the pure
 * `cleanupMerit` helper but ZERO tests calling `main()` end-to-end. Production
 * apply on 2026-06-16 destroyed 13 character documents because main()'s
 * `find({}, {projection: {_id, name, merits}})` + `replaceOne({_id}, doc)`
 * combination overwrote each character with the projected shape, deleting
 * every unprojected field (attributes / skills / disciplines / clan /
 * covenant / status / xp / humanity / blood_potency / aspirations / etc).
 *
 * Same blind-spot class as N-7c (orchestrator dispatch missing) — helpers
 * tested in isolation, integration path not. Memory:
 * `feedback_script_integration_test` pins the discipline: any data-mutating
 * script needs ≥1 test calling main() end-to-end with real DB writes
 * (not just the pure helpers).
 *
 * This test:
 *   1. Seeds a character with attributes + skills + disciplines + clan +
 *      covenant + contaminated merits
 *   2. Sets process.argv to include '--apply' + sets MONGODB_URI to the
 *      test db
 *   3. Calls main() end-to-end
 *   4. Reads the doc back via getCollection
 *   5. Asserts ALL unrelated fields survive AND merits are cleaned
 *
 * The post-#826 fix (updateOne + $set: merits) makes assertions 5a (survival)
 * AND 5b (cleanup) both pass. The pre-#826 shape (replaceOne with projected
 * doc) would have stripped attributes / skills / etc — assertion 5a fails.
 * This test would have caught the bug before deploy.
 */

import { describe, it, expect, beforeAll, afterAll, beforeEach } from 'vitest';
import 'dotenv/config';
import { setupDb, teardownDb } from './helpers/db-setup.js';
import { getCollection } from '../db.js';
import { main } from '../scripts/cleanup-free-channel-contamination.js';

const TEST_FLAG = '_issue_826_integration_test';

beforeAll(async () => {
  await setupDb();
});

afterAll(async () => {
  // Clean up any test residue.
  const col = getCollection('characters');
  await col.deleteMany({ [TEST_FLAG]: true });
  await teardownDb();
});

beforeEach(async () => {
  // Belt-and-braces — each test starts clean.
  const col = getCollection('characters');
  await col.deleteMany({ [TEST_FLAG]: true });
});

// Fully-formed seed character with EVERY top-level field the editor writes,
// so the integration assertion can confirm none is silently dropped.
function seedDoc() {
  return {
    [TEST_FLAG]: true,
    name: '#826 Integration Test',
    clan: 'Nosferatu',
    covenant: 'Invictus',
    mask: 'Survivor',
    dirge: 'Curmudgeon',
    bloodline: null,
    concept: 'Integration test fixture',
    status: { city: 1, clan: 2, covenant: 3 },
    attributes: {
      Intelligence: { dots: 3, bonus: 0 },
      Wits: { dots: 2, bonus: 0 },
      Resolve: { dots: 2, bonus: 0 },
      Strength: { dots: 2, bonus: 0 },
      Dexterity: { dots: 3, bonus: 0 },
      Stamina: { dots: 2, bonus: 0 },
      Presence: { dots: 1, bonus: 0 },
      Manipulation: { dots: 2, bonus: 0 },
      Composure: { dots: 3, bonus: 0 },
    },
    skills: {
      Investigation: { dots: 3, bonus: 0, specs: ['Forensics'], nine_again: false },
      Stealth: { dots: 4, bonus: 0, specs: [], nine_again: false },
      Larceny: { dots: 2, bonus: 0, specs: [], nine_again: false },
    },
    disciplines: { Auspex: 2, Obfuscate: 3, Vigour: 1 },
    powers: [],
    humanity: 6,
    humanity_base: 7,
    blood_potency: 1,
    xp_log: { spent: 0, earned: 10 },
    attr_creation: 5,
    skill_creation: 11,
    disc_creation: 0,
    merit_creation: 0,
    ordeals: [],
    aspirations: ['Survive the night'],
    touchstones: [],
    devotions: [],
    fighting_styles: [],
    rites: [],
    pacts: [],
    equipment: [],
    notes: 'seeded by #826 integration test',
    // Contaminated merits — Pattern A on Catacombs, Pattern B on Allies.
    merits: [
      { name: 'Necropolis Sepulcher', category: 'domain', cp: 3, xp: 0 },
      { name: 'Catacombs', category: 'domain', cp: 0, xp: 0, free: 1, free_grants: { necro: 1 } }, // Pattern A
      { name: 'Allies', category: 'influence', cp: 0, xp: 0, free_mci: 3, free_grants: { mci: 3 } }, // Pattern B
      { name: 'Safe Place', category: 'domain', cp: 2, xp: 0, qualifier: 'Apt' }, // untouched control
    ],
  };
}

describe('#826 — cleanup script main() integration (write-path safety)', () => {
  it('preserves ALL non-merits fields when --apply runs against a contaminated character', async () => {
    const col = getCollection('characters');
    const seed = seedDoc();
    const ins = await col.insertOne(seed);
    const id = ins.insertedId;

    // Snapshot the seed for post-run comparison (use the inserted doc shape).
    const before = await col.findOne({ _id: id });

    // Toggle APPLY mode for this run; ensure MONGODB_URI is set so main()
    // doesn't exit. setupDb has already established the connection via the
    // shared db.js, so MONGODB_URI is in process.env.
    const origArgv = process.argv;
    process.argv = [...origArgv, '--apply'];
    try {
      await main();
    } finally {
      process.argv = origArgv;
    }

    const after = await col.findOne({ _id: id });

    // ── Survival assertions — the core safety check ──────────────────────
    // Pre-#826: replaceOne overwrote with the projected doc (only _id, name,
    // merits). These assertions would have ALL failed. Post-#826: $set: merits
    // leaves the rest untouched.
    expect(after.clan, 'clan must survive').toBe(before.clan);
    expect(after.covenant, 'covenant must survive').toBe(before.covenant);
    expect(after.mask, 'mask must survive').toBe(before.mask);
    expect(after.dirge, 'dirge must survive').toBe(before.dirge);
    expect(after.concept, 'concept must survive').toBe(before.concept);
    expect(after.status, 'status must survive').toEqual(before.status);
    expect(after.attributes, 'attributes must survive (this is the field the prod incident lost)').toEqual(before.attributes);
    expect(after.skills, 'skills must survive').toEqual(before.skills);
    expect(after.disciplines, 'disciplines must survive').toEqual(before.disciplines);
    expect(after.humanity, 'humanity must survive').toBe(before.humanity);
    expect(after.humanity_base, 'humanity_base must survive').toBe(before.humanity_base);
    expect(after.blood_potency, 'blood_potency must survive').toBe(before.blood_potency);
    expect(after.xp_log, 'xp_log must survive').toEqual(before.xp_log);
    expect(after.attr_creation, 'attr_creation must survive').toBe(before.attr_creation);
    expect(after.skill_creation, 'skill_creation must survive').toBe(before.skill_creation);
    expect(after.aspirations, 'aspirations must survive').toEqual(before.aspirations);
    expect(after.notes, 'notes must survive').toBe(before.notes);

    // ── Cleanup assertions — merits ARE modified per the script's purpose ──
    const cat = after.merits.find(m => m.name === 'Catacombs');
    expect(cat, 'Catacombs row must remain').toBeTruthy();
    expect(cat.free, 'Pattern A: m.free zeroed').toBe(0);
    expect(cat.free_grants.necro, 'Catacombs map.necro preserved').toBe(1);

    const allies = after.merits.find(m => m.name === 'Allies');
    expect(allies, 'Allies row must remain').toBeTruthy();
    expect(allies.free_mci, 'Pattern B: legacy free_mci zeroed').toBe(0);
    expect(allies.free_grants.mci, 'Allies map.mci preserved').toBe(3);

    const sepulcher = after.merits.find(m => m.name === 'Necropolis Sepulcher');
    expect(sepulcher, 'Sepulcher (untouched control) must remain').toBeTruthy();
    expect(sepulcher.cp, 'Sepulcher cp preserved').toBe(3);

    const safePlace = after.merits.find(m => m.name === 'Safe Place');
    expect(safePlace, 'Safe Place (untouched control) must remain').toBeTruthy();
    expect(safePlace.qualifier, 'Safe Place qualifier preserved').toBe('Apt');
  });

  it('dry-run mode does not modify the document (no --apply flag)', async () => {
    const col = getCollection('characters');
    const seed = seedDoc();
    const ins = await col.insertOne(seed);
    const id = ins.insertedId;
    const before = await col.findOne({ _id: id });

    // No --apply flag → dry run.
    const origArgv = process.argv;
    process.argv = origArgv.filter(a => a !== '--apply');
    try {
      await main();
    } finally {
      process.argv = origArgv;
    }

    const after = await col.findOne({ _id: id });
    // Whole doc unchanged.
    expect(after).toEqual(before);
  });

  it('idempotent: running main() twice with --apply leaves the doc unchanged on the second run', async () => {
    const col = getCollection('characters');
    const seed = seedDoc();
    const ins = await col.insertOne(seed);
    const id = ins.insertedId;

    const origArgv = process.argv;
    process.argv = [...origArgv, '--apply'];
    try {
      await main();
      const afterFirst = await col.findOne({ _id: id });
      await main();
      const afterSecond = await col.findOne({ _id: id });
      // Second run finds no contamination, makes no writes — docs identical.
      expect(afterSecond).toEqual(afterFirst);
      // And the survival assertions still hold across both runs.
      expect(afterSecond.attributes).toBeTruthy();
      expect(afterSecond.skills).toBeTruthy();
      expect(afterSecond.disciplines).toBeTruthy();
    } finally {
      process.argv = origArgv;
    }
  });
});

/**
 * Test coverage for issue #823 — defence-in-depth guards against tests
 * accidentally connecting to the production database.
 *
 * Root cause: a regression once let test runs leak writes into prod
 * ("Regent Save Test" territory pollution, June 2026). Two guards now exist:
 *
 * 1. server/db.js connectDb() — refuses to connect if VITEST is set and the
 *    resolved DB name doesn't end with `_test` (checked via the exported
 *    pure function assertTestDbSafety, before client.connect() ever runs).
 * 2. server/tests/helpers/db-setup.js setupDb() — re-asserts the connected
 *    database name ends with `_test` after connectDb() resolves, catching
 *    the case where a connection was already established before
 *    setup-env.js's override took effect.
 */

import { describe, it, expect, beforeAll, afterAll } from 'vitest';
import { assertTestDbSafety, getDb } from '../db.js';
import { setupDb, teardownDb } from './helpers/db-setup.js';

beforeAll(async () => {
  await setupDb();
});

afterAll(async () => {
  await teardownDb();
});

describe('issue #823 — vitest run is actually on the test DB', () => {
  it('getDb().databaseName is tm_suite_test (proves setup-env.js plumbing held)', () => {
    expect(getDb().databaseName).toBe('tm_suite_test');
  });
});

describe('issue #823 — guard 1: assertTestDbSafety (db.js connectDb decision logic)', () => {
  it('vitest + prod-shaped name → throws', () => {
    expect(() => assertTestDbSafety('tm_suite', true)).toThrow(
      /Refusing to connect: test context \(VITEST\) targeting non-test database 'tm_suite'/
    );
  });

  it('vitest + test-shaped name → does not throw', () => {
    expect(() => assertTestDbSafety('tm_suite_test', true)).not.toThrow();
  });

  it('non-vitest + prod-shaped name → does not throw (scripts/prod unaffected)', () => {
    expect(() => assertTestDbSafety('tm_suite', false)).not.toThrow();
  });

  it('non-vitest + test-shaped name → does not throw', () => {
    expect(() => assertTestDbSafety('tm_suite_test', false)).not.toThrow();
  });
});

describe('issue #823 — guard 2: setupDb() re-assertion', () => {
  it('resolves cleanly in the current (correct) environment', async () => {
    await expect(setupDb()).resolves.toBeUndefined();
  });

  it('the connected database name actually satisfies the guard 2 assertion the code checks', () => {
    // Honest check, not a fake assert: re-run the exact predicate setupDb()
    // uses (dbName.endsWith('_test')) against the live connection it produced.
    const dbName = getDb().databaseName;
    expect(dbName.endsWith('_test')).toBe(true);
  });
});

/**
 * Test DB setup/teardown — connects to real MongoDB for integration tests.
 */

import { connectDb, closeDb, getCollection, getDb } from '../../db.js';

export async function setupDb() {
  try {
    await connectDb(); // No-op if already connected (idempotent)
  } catch (err) {
    console.error('[setupDb] connectDb() failed:', err.message);
    throw err;
  }

  // Belt-and-braces: catches the case where a connection was already
  // established (by earlier-running code) before setup-env.js's override
  // took effect. connectDb()'s own guard only fires on the connection that
  // creates `db`; this re-checks whatever connection setupDb() ends up with.
  const dbName = getDb().databaseName;
  if (!dbName.endsWith('_test')) {
    throw new Error(
      `Refusing test run: connected database '${dbName}' does not end with '_test'. ` +
        `Tests must use a *_test database — check tests/helpers/setup-env.js ordering.`
    );
  }
}

export async function teardownDb() {
  // No-op — closing mid-run causes failures when test files share a process.
  // The connection closes naturally when the process exits.
}

/**
 * issue-1143 (AC5): non-throwing connectivity probe, for suites that want a
 * clean vitest skip rather than a failed beforeAll + a second erroring
 * afterAll cleanup. setupDb() itself keeps its existing throw-on-failure
 * contract unchanged (other suites already depend on that shape) — this is
 * a separate, additive helper. Usage:
 *
 *   const dbAvailable = await isDbAvailable();
 *   describe.skipIf(!dbAvailable)('suite name', () => {
 *     beforeAll(async () => { await setupDb(); ... });
 *     ...
 *   });
 *
 * The top-level `await` works because vitest test files are ESM modules.
 */
export async function isDbAvailable() {
  try {
    await setupDb();
    return true;
  } catch {
    return false;
  }
}

/**
 * Get a few character IDs for testing player filtering.
 *
 * Against tm_suite_test (the default under vitest), the characters collection
 * is usually empty. Auto-seed minimal stub characters when we don't have
 * enough, so tests that just need "some valid character IDs" work without
 * every test file having to roll its own fixtures.
 */
export async function getTestCharacterIds(count = 2) {
  const col = getCollection('characters');
  let chars = await col
    .find({ retired: { $ne: true } })
    .limit(count)
    .project({ _id: 1, name: 1 })
    .toArray();

  if (chars.length < count) {
    const need = count - chars.length;
    const stubs = Array.from({ length: need }, (_, i) => ({
      name: `Test Character ${Date.now()}_${i}`,
      retired: false,
      _test_seeded: true,
    }));
    const result = await col.insertMany(stubs);
    const seededIds = Object.values(result.insertedIds);
    const seededDocs = await col
      .find({ _id: { $in: seededIds } })
      .project({ _id: 1, name: 1 })
      .toArray();
    chars = [...chars, ...seededDocs];
  }

  return chars.map(c => ({ id: c._id.toString(), name: c.name }));
}

+# Adversarial review — oxp-1
+
+## High
+
+- **[Pass 1] The purported ISO-date guard accepts impossible dates and malformed timestamps.** Severity: High. File: `server/schemas/office_seat.schema.js:76`; mirrored in `server/scripts/seed-office-seats.mjs:109`. Trigger: supply Rene's required override as `2026-99-99` (or a syntactically matching timestamp such as `2026-02-21T+++`). Observable consequence: `buildSeatDocs` accepts the value and an `--apply` run can persist it to the live collection even though downstream date arithmetic can produce `NaN`, exactly the silent bad-XP outcome the guard says it prevents; the schema accepts the same bad value. The tests cover prose (`21 February 2026`) but no calendar-invalid matching value. Confidence: High (direct regex analysis; no script or database invocation).
+
+## Medium
+
+- **[Pass 1] The seed is only sequentially idempotent; concurrent applies can insert duplicate natural keys.** Severity: Medium. File: `server/scripts/seed-office-seats.mjs:167-189`. Trigger: two `seedOfficeSeats(..., { apply: true })` calls overlap so both `findOne({ office_category, holder_id })` operations for a seat finish before either `insertOne`. Observable consequence: both calls insert a document for the same purported natural key because the diff adds neither an atomic upsert nor a unique compound index. The only idempotency test calls the function twice sequentially, so the unqualified doc-comment claim “Idempotent by the natural key” and the rerun guidance do not cover this race. Confidence: High (direct control-flow analysis).
+
+## Low
+
+- **[Pass 1] Bare invocation establishes a live connection before rejecting the missing Rene date.** Severity: Low. File: `server/scripts/seed-office-seats.mjs:204-230`. Trigger: invoke the script with zero flags in the documented `server/.env` environment. Observable consequence: argument parsing selects dry-run and a null Rene date, but `main` calls `connectDb()` before `seedOfficeSeats` calls `buildSeatDocs` and throws; this makes no collection query or write, but does contact live Atlas, so the strongest safe failure would validate arguments before connecting and the “dry-run default is what makes that safe” wording omits the avoidable live connection. Confidence: High (direct control-flow analysis; invocation was forbidden and not attempted).
+
+- **[Pass 1] The “second validator” precaution neither creates a second validator nor is needed for these assertions.** Severity: Low. File: `server/tests/oxp-1-office-seats.test.js:193-221`. Trigger: run any N-seats-per-office schema test. Observable consequence: `ajv.compile(officeSeatSchema)` on the same schema object is cached by AJV and can return the same validation function; moreover each assertion evaluates its validation result and `.errors` message before the next validation call, so no later call can overwrite the earlier assertion's message. The tests still prove both individual documents validate, but the comments overstate a simultaneous-validation safeguard and do not themselves prove collection coexistence (the later DB tests do when they run). Confidence: Medium-High (AJV caching semantics plus JavaScript argument evaluation; repository/AJV version not yet opened in this pass).
+
+- **[Pass 1] The stored-document round-trip test only validates a hand-stringified surrogate.** Severity: Low. File: `server/schemas/office_seat.schema.js:86`; `server/tests/oxp-1-office-seats.test.js:101-105,375-379`. Trigger: pass a raw MongoDB document, whose `_id` and non-null `holder_id` are BSON `ObjectId` instances, directly to the schema validator. Observable consequence: both fields fail the schema's string typing; the DB-backed test avoids this by explicitly converting both values with `String(...)`, and the nominal round-trip test constructs `_id` as a string from the outset. That may be the intended JSON boundary, but the diff contains no consumer establishing it, so the test title does not prove a raw stored document round-trips. Confidence: High about the mismatch; Medium about impact because the diff intentionally adds no consumer.

+# Adversarial review — oxp-1
+
+## High
+
+- **[Pass 1] The purported ISO-date guard accepts impossible dates and malformed timestamps.** Severity: High. File: `server/schemas/office_seat.schema.js:76`; mirrored in `server/scripts/seed-office-seats.mjs:109`. Trigger: supply Rene's required override as `2026-99-99` (or a syntactically matching timestamp such as `2026-02-21T+++`). Observable consequence: `buildSeatDocs` accepts the value and an `--apply` run can persist it to the live collection even though downstream date arithmetic can produce `NaN`, exactly the silent bad-XP outcome the guard says it prevents; the schema accepts the same bad value. The tests cover prose (`21 February 2026`) but no calendar-invalid matching value. Confidence: High (direct regex analysis; no script or database invocation).
+
+## Medium
+
+- **[Pass 1] The seed is only sequentially idempotent; concurrent applies can insert duplicate natural keys.** Severity: Medium. File: `server/scripts/seed-office-seats.mjs:167-189`. Trigger: two `seedOfficeSeats(..., { apply: true })` calls overlap so both `findOne({ office_category, holder_id })` operations for a seat finish before either `insertOne`. Observable consequence: both calls insert a document for the same purported natural key because the diff adds neither an atomic upsert nor a unique compound index. The only idempotency test calls the function twice sequentially, so the unqualified doc-comment claim “Idempotent by the natural key” and the rerun guidance do not cover this race. Confidence: High (direct control-flow analysis).
+
+## Low
+
+- **[Pass 1] Bare invocation establishes a live connection before rejecting the missing Rene date.** Severity: Low. File: `server/scripts/seed-office-seats.mjs:204-230`. Trigger: invoke the script with zero flags in the documented `server/.env` environment. Observable consequence: argument parsing selects dry-run and a null Rene date, but `main` calls `connectDb()` before `seedOfficeSeats` calls `buildSeatDocs` and throws; this makes no collection query or write, but does contact live Atlas, so the strongest safe failure would validate arguments before connecting and the “dry-run default is what makes that safe” wording omits the avoidable live connection. Confidence: High (direct control-flow analysis; invocation was forbidden and not attempted).
+
+- **[Pass 1] The “second validator” precaution neither creates a second validator nor is needed for these assertions.** Severity: Low. File: `server/tests/oxp-1-office-seats.test.js:193-221`. Trigger: run any N-seats-per-office schema test. Observable consequence: `ajv.compile(officeSeatSchema)` on the same schema object is cached by AJV and can return the same validation function; moreover each assertion evaluates its validation result and `.errors` message before the next validation call, so no later call can overwrite the earlier assertion's message. The tests still prove both individual documents validate, but the comments overstate a simultaneous-validation safeguard and do not themselves prove collection coexistence (the later DB tests do when they run). Confidence: Medium-High (AJV caching semantics plus JavaScript argument evaluation; repository/AJV version not yet opened in this pass).
+
+- **[Pass 1] The stored-document round-trip test only validates a hand-stringified surrogate.** Severity: Low. File: `server/schemas/office_seat.schema.js:86`; `server/tests/oxp-1-office-seats.test.js:101-105,375-379`. Trigger: pass a raw MongoDB document, whose `_id` and non-null `holder_id` are BSON `ObjectId` instances, directly to the schema validator. Observable consequence: both fields fail the schema's string typing; the DB-backed test avoids this by explicitly converting both values with `String(...)`, and the nominal round-trip test constructs `_id` as a string from the outset. That may be the intended JSON boundary, but the diff contains no consumer establishing it, so the test title does not prove a raw stored document round-trips. Confidence: High about the mismatch; Medium about impact because the diff intentionally adds no consumer.
+
+## Pass 1 validation notes (frozen before Pass 2)
+
+- Opened only `specs/stories/code-review/oxp-1-diff.txt`, in three line ranges after the first whole-file output was truncated by the command wrapper. I did not open repository source, the story, sprint status, or the output path before creating this file.

+- I did not execute any test or application code in Pass 1. I did not invoke `server/scripts/seed-office-seats.mjs`, connect to MongoDB, or read any `.env` file.

+# Adversarial review — oxp-1
+
+## High
+
+- **[Pass 1] The purported ISO-date guard accepts impossible dates and malformed timestamps.** Severity: High. File: `server/schemas/office_seat.schema.js:76`; mirrored in `server/scripts/seed-office-seats.mjs:109`. Trigger: supply Rene's required override as `2026-99-99` (or a syntactically matching timestamp such as `2026-02-21T+++`). Observable consequence: `buildSeatDocs` accepts the value and an `--apply` run can persist it to the live collection even though downstream date arithmetic can produce `NaN`, exactly the silent bad-XP outcome the guard says it prevents; the schema accepts the same bad value. The tests cover prose (`21 February 2026`) but no calendar-invalid matching value. Confidence: High (direct regex analysis; no script or database invocation).
+
+## Medium
+
+- **[Pass 1] The seed is only sequentially idempotent; concurrent applies can insert duplicate natural keys.** Severity: Medium. File: `server/scripts/seed-office-seats.mjs:167-189`. Trigger: two `seedOfficeSeats(..., { apply: true })` calls overlap so both `findOne({ office_category, holder_id })` operations for a seat finish before either `insertOne`. Observable consequence: both calls insert a document for the same purported natural key because the diff adds neither an atomic upsert nor a unique compound index. The only idempotency test calls the function twice sequentially, so the unqualified doc-comment claim “Idempotent by the natural key” and the rerun guidance do not cover this race. Confidence: High (direct control-flow analysis).
+
+## Low
+
+- **[Pass 1] Bare invocation establishes a live connection before rejecting the missing Rene date.** Severity: Low. File: `server/scripts/seed-office-seats.mjs:204-230`. Trigger: invoke the script with zero flags in the documented `server/.env` environment. Observable consequence: argument parsing selects dry-run and a null Rene date, but `main` calls `connectDb()` before `seedOfficeSeats` calls `buildSeatDocs` and throws; this makes no collection query or write, but does contact live Atlas, so the strongest safe failure would validate arguments before connecting and the “dry-run default is what makes that safe” wording omits the avoidable live connection. Confidence: High (direct control-flow analysis; invocation was forbidden and not attempted).
+
+- **[Pass 1] The “second validator” precaution neither creates a second validator nor is needed for these assertions.** Severity: Low. File: `server/tests/oxp-1-office-seats.test.js:193-221`. Trigger: run any N-seats-per-office schema test. Observable consequence: `ajv.compile(officeSeatSchema)` on the same schema object is cached by AJV and can return the same validation function; moreover each assertion evaluates its validation result and `.errors` message before the next validation call, so no later call can overwrite the earlier assertion's message. The tests still prove both individual documents validate, but the comments overstate a simultaneous-validation safeguard and do not themselves prove collection coexistence (the later DB tests do when they run). Confidence: Medium-High (AJV caching semantics plus JavaScript argument evaluation; repository/AJV version not yet opened in this pass).
+
+- **[Pass 1] The stored-document round-trip test only validates a hand-stringified surrogate.** Severity: Low. File: `server/schemas/office_seat.schema.js:86`; `server/tests/oxp-1-office-seats.test.js:101-105,375-379`. Trigger: pass a raw MongoDB document, whose `_id` and non-null `holder_id` are BSON `ObjectId` instances, directly to the schema validator. Observable consequence: both fields fail the schema's string typing; the DB-backed test avoids this by explicitly converting both values with `String(...)`, and the nominal round-trip test constructs `_id` as a string from the outset. That may be the intended JSON boundary, but the diff contains no consumer establishing it, so the test title does not prove a raw stored document round-trips. Confidence: High about the mismatch; Medium about impact because the diff intentionally adds no consumer.
+

/**
 * Generic JSON Schema validation middleware factory.
 *
 * Usage:
 *   import { validate } from '../middleware/validate.js';
 *   import { playerSchema } from '../schemas/player.schema.js';
 *   router.post('/', validate(playerSchema), async (req, res) => { ... });
 *
 * Returns 400 with structured error list on validation failure.
 * Passes through to next() on success.
 */

import Ajv from 'ajv';

const ajv = new Ajv({ allErrors: true, coerceTypes: false });

// Cache compiled validators by schema title to avoid recompilation
const cache = new Map();

export function validate(schema) {
  let compiledValidate = cache.get(schema.title);
  if (!compiledValidate) {
    compiledValidate = ajv.compile(schema);
    cache.set(schema.title, compiledValidate);
  }

  return (req, res, next) => {
    const valid = compiledValidate(req.body);
    if (valid) return next();

    const errors = compiledValidate.errors.map(e => ({
      path:    e.instancePath || '(root)',
      message: e.message,
      ...(e.params?.additionalProperty
        ? { property: e.params.additionalProperty }
        : {}),
    }));

    return res.status(400).json({
      error:   'VALIDATION_ERROR',
      message: `Request body failed schema validation (${errors.length} error${errors.length === 1 ? '' : 's'})`,
      errors,
    });
  };
}

+# Adversarial review — oxp-1
+
+## High
+
+- **[Pass 1] The purported ISO-date guard accepts impossible dates and malformed timestamps.** Severity: High. File: `server/schemas/office_seat.schema.js:76`; mirrored in `server/scripts/seed-office-seats.mjs:109`. Trigger: supply Rene's required override as `2026-99-99` (or a syntactically matching timestamp such as `2026-02-21T+++`). Observable consequence: `buildSeatDocs` accepts the value and an `--apply` run can persist it to the live collection even though downstream date arithmetic can produce `NaN`, exactly the silent bad-XP outcome the guard says it prevents; the schema accepts the same bad value. The tests cover prose (`21 February 2026`) but no calendar-invalid matching value. Confidence: High (direct regex analysis; no script or database invocation).
+
+## Medium
+
+- **[Pass 1] The seed is only sequentially idempotent; concurrent applies can insert duplicate natural keys.** Severity: Medium. File: `server/scripts/seed-office-seats.mjs:167-189`. Trigger: two `seedOfficeSeats(..., { apply: true })` calls overlap so both `findOne({ office_category, holder_id })` operations for a seat finish before either `insertOne`. Observable consequence: both calls insert a document for the same purported natural key because the diff adds neither an atomic upsert nor a unique compound index. The only idempotency test calls the function twice sequentially, so the unqualified doc-comment claim “Idempotent by the natural key” and the rerun guidance do not cover this race. Confidence: High (direct control-flow analysis).
+
+## Low
+
+- **[Pass 1] Bare invocation establishes a live connection before rejecting the missing Rene date.** Severity: Low. File: `server/scripts/seed-office-seats.mjs:204-230`. Trigger: invoke the script with zero flags in the documented `server/.env` environment. Observable consequence: argument parsing selects dry-run and a null Rene date, but `main` calls `connectDb()` before `seedOfficeSeats` calls `buildSeatDocs` and throws; this makes no collection query or write, but does contact live Atlas, so the strongest safe failure would validate arguments before connecting and the “dry-run default is what makes that safe” wording omits the avoidable live connection. Confidence: High (direct control-flow analysis; invocation was forbidden and not attempted).
+
+- **[Pass 1] The “second validator” precaution neither creates a second validator nor is needed for these assertions.** Severity: Low. File: `server/tests/oxp-1-office-seats.test.js:193-221`. Trigger: run any N-seats-per-office schema test. Observable consequence: `ajv.compile(officeSeatSchema)` on the same schema object is cached by AJV and can return the same validation function; moreover each assertion evaluates its validation result and `.errors` message before the next validation call, so no later call can overwrite the earlier assertion's message. The tests still prove both individual documents validate, but the comments overstate a simultaneous-validation safeguard and do not themselves prove collection coexistence (the later DB tests do when they run). Confidence: Medium-High (AJV caching semantics plus JavaScript argument evaluation; repository/AJV version not yet opened in this pass).
+
+- **[Pass 1] The stored-document round-trip test only validates a hand-stringified surrogate.** Severity: Low. File: `server/schemas/office_seat.schema.js:86`; `server/tests/oxp-1-office-seats.test.js:101-105,375-379`. Trigger: pass a raw MongoDB document, whose `_id` and non-null `holder_id` are BSON `ObjectId` instances, directly to the schema validator. Observable consequence: both fields fail the schema's string typing; the DB-backed test avoids this by explicitly converting both values with `String(...)`, and the nominal round-trip test constructs `_id` as a string from the outset. That may be the intended JSON boundary, but the diff contains no consumer establishing it, so the test title does not prove a raw stored document round-trips. Confidence: High about the mismatch; Medium about impact because the diff intentionally adds no consumer.
+
+## Pass 1 validation notes (frozen before Pass 2)
+
+- Opened only `specs/stories/code-review/oxp-1-diff.txt`, in three line ranges after the first whole-file output was truncated by the command wrapper. I did not open repository source, the story, sprint status, or the output path before creating this file.

+## Pass 2 validation notes (frozen before Pass 3)

+- Opened in full: `server/tests/helpers/setup-env.js`, `server/db.js`, `server/tests/helpers/db-setup.js`, `server/vitest.config.js`, `server/package.json`, `server/scripts/backfill-free-grants.js`, `server/tests/issue-823-test-db-guard.test.js`, `server/tests/issue-826-cleanup-script-integration.test.js`, `server/middleware/validate.js`, and `server/schemas/downtime_submission.schema.js` (the latter re-opened in three numbered chunks after a combined command was truncated). +- Test-DB safety result: `server/vitest.config.js` installs `tests/helpers/setup-env.js` as `setupFiles` before test modules; that file unconditionally assigns `process.env.MONGODB_DB = 'tm_suite_test'`. `connectDb()` resolves that environment value and calls `assertTestDbSafety` before constructing/connecting `MongoClient`; under Vitest, any non-`_test` name throws. `setupDb()` independently checks `getDb().databaseName.endsWith('_test')` after connection, including an already-open connection. A test-source search found no `MongoClient` import/use and no mutation of `VITEST`; the one existing test that imports a script with its own Mongo client (`issue-826-cleanup-script-integration.test.js`) imports it after setup has forced `MONGODB_DB`, and that script resolves its DB name from the forced environment. Thus the existing Vitest DB paths cannot resolve production through the configuration or code path identified. This is a guarantee about the repository's existing harness and test code, not a claim that a newly malicious test could not deliberately bypass project helpers and hard-code a production connection.
+- Enum result: direct comparison printed `OFFICE_CATEGORY_ENUM` and `characterSchema.properties.court_category.enum`; after removing only `''` and `null`, order and character-for-character contents were exactly equal: `Head of State`, `Primogen`, `Administrator`, `Socialite`, `Enforcer`.
+- Precedent result: `downtime_submission.schema.js:62-64` really uses a lowercase-only 24-hex ObjectId string pattern (plus its intentional empty-string case), and lines 231-235 really document that the project lacks `ajv-formats` and therefore uses a string instead of `format: 'date-time'`. `backfill-free-grants.js` uses the same dotenv-first import, `connectDb`/`getCollection`/`closeDb` imports, connect/`try`/`finally`/close lifecycle, environment/default DB reporting, and direct-invocation guard as the new seed script.
+- Consumer sweep result: the complete tracked-source search (excluding the deliberately unopened oxp-1 story/review artifacts) found no reference outside the three new source/test files. +# Adversarial review — oxp-1
+
+## High
+
+- **[Pass 1] The purported ISO-date guard accepts impossible dates and malformed timestamps.** Severity: High. File: `server/schemas/office_seat.schema.js:76`; mirrored in `server/scripts/seed-office-seats.mjs:109`. Trigger: supply Rene's required override as `2026-99-99` (or a syntactically matching timestamp such as `2026-02-21T+++`). Observable consequence: `buildSeatDocs` accepts the value and an `--apply` run can persist it to the live collection even though downstream date arithmetic can produce `NaN`, exactly the silent bad-XP outcome the guard says it prevents; the schema accepts the same bad value. The tests cover prose (`21 February 2026`) but no calendar-invalid matching value. Confidence: High (direct regex analysis; no script or database invocation).
+
+## Medium
+
+- **[Pass 1] The seed is only sequentially idempotent; concurrent applies can insert duplicate natural keys.** Severity: Medium. File: `server/scripts/seed-office-seats.mjs:167-189`. Trigger: two `seedOfficeSeats(..., { apply: true })` calls overlap so both `findOne({ office_category, holder_id })` operations for a seat finish before either `insertOne`. Observable consequence: both calls insert a document for the same purported natural key because the diff adds neither an atomic upsert nor a unique compound index. The only idempotency test calls the function twice sequentially, so the unqualified doc-comment claim “Idempotent by the natural key” and the rerun guidance do not cover this race. Confidence: High (direct control-flow analysis).
+
+## Low
+
+- **[Pass 1] Bare invocation establishes a live connection before rejecting the missing Rene date.** Severity: Low. File: `server/scripts/seed-office-seats.mjs:204-230`. Trigger: invoke the script with zero flags in the documented `server/.env` environment. Observable consequence: argument parsing selects dry-run and a null Rene date, but `main` calls `connectDb()` before `seedOfficeSeats` calls `buildSeatDocs` and throws; this makes no collection query or write, but does contact live Atlas, so the strongest safe failure would validate arguments before connecting and the “dry-run default is what makes that safe” wording omits the avoidable live connection. Confidence: High (direct control-flow analysis; invocation was forbidden and not attempted).
+
+- **[Pass 1] The “second validator” precaution neither creates a second validator nor is needed for these assertions.** Severity: Low. File: `server/tests/oxp-1-office-seats.test.js:193-221`. Trigger: run any N-seats-per-office schema test. Observable consequence: `ajv.compile(officeSeatSchema)` on the same schema object is cached by AJV and can return the same validation function; moreover each assertion evaluates its validation result and `.errors` message before the next validation call, so no later call can overwrite the earlier assertion's message. The tests still prove both individual documents validate, but the comments overstate a simultaneous-validation safeguard and do not themselves prove collection coexistence (the later DB tests do when they run). Confidence: Medium-High (AJV caching semantics plus JavaScript argument evaluation; repository/AJV version not yet opened in this pass).
+
+- **[Pass 1] The stored-document round-trip test only validates a hand-stringified surrogate.** Severity: Low. File: `server/schemas/office_seat.schema.js:86`; `server/tests/oxp-1-office-seats.test.js:101-105,375-379`. Trigger: pass a raw MongoDB document, whose `_id` and non-null `holder_id` are BSON `ObjectId` instances, directly to the schema validator. Observable consequence: both fields fail the schema's string typing; the DB-backed test avoids this by explicitly converting both values with `String(...)`, and the nominal round-trip test constructs `_id` as a string from the outset. That may be the intended JSON boundary, but the diff contains no consumer establishing it, so the test title does not prove a raw stored document round-trips. Confidence: High about the mismatch; Medium about impact because the diff intentionally adds no consumer.

   6: 
   7: ## Story
   8: 
   9: As the ST team,
  10: I want a real seat-keyed data model for office/seat data, seeded with the actual current holders and
  11: their real creation dates,
  12: so that Epic OXP's remaining stories (oxp.2 derived XP, oxp.5 handover, oxp.6 purchase markers,
  13: oxp.7 sheet section) have a stable foundation to build on, instead of continuing to infer seat
  14: identity from `court_category` alone — which cannot currently distinguish two people holding the
  15: same office at once.
  16: 
  17: ## Why this story exists, and what changed before it was written
  18: 
  19: This is Epic OXP's own designated "data-lock" story. Per this project's convention (`bmad-data-lock`
  20: skill), the data-lock investigation ran as a real pass against live `tm_suite` MongoDB data
  21: **before** this story was written, not as an assumption folded into the spec after the fact. Full
  22: findings are in `data-map.md` (umbrella root, `D:\Terra Mortis\data-map.md`); this section carries
  23: forward only what shapes the story.
  24: 
  25: **Finding 1 — `game_sessions` is not uniquely keyed by `game_number`.** Live data has 5 documents
  26: each for `game_number: 3` and `game_number: 4` — 1 real, 4 junk placeholders. For game 3 the real
  27: document is the OLDEST of the five, not the newest. See `data-map.md` Known Drift Pattern #17.
  28: 
  29: **Finding 2 — seat multiplicity is not confined to Socialite. Ruled by Angelus, 2026-08-13.** The
  30: epic (`specs/epic-oxp-office-xp-economy.md`, dev branch only) states only Socialite has two
  31: concurrent seats. Live data showed Primogen ALSO currently has two simultaneous holders — Yusuf
  32: Kalusicj and René St. Dominique, both `court_title: 'Primogen'` (identical, unlike Socialite's two
  33: distinct titles: "Harpy" / "People's Harpy"). Raised directly to Angelus during the data-lock; his
  34: ruling: **"you can have more than one Primogen"** — this is real, not a data-hygiene bug. The epic's
  35: "only Socialite has two seats" framing is therefore itself corrected: **any office can have N
  36: concurrent seats**, not just Socialite. This story's schema must key seats generically, never
  37: special-case one office name.
  38: 
  39: **Finding 3 — the seat-collision risk oxp.3/oxp.4 waved off is now proven live, not hypothetical.**
  40: `office_merit_dots`/`office_manoeuvre_rank` (shipped by oxp-3/oxp-4) are keyed purely by office
  41: category. Socialite's two real seats (Brandy LaRoux / Carver) would silently share the single
  42: `_id: 'Socialite'` document the instant either gets a real merit or manoeuvre-rank purchase — there
  43: is no way today to tell whose purchase is whose. **Deliberate scope decision for this story: do NOT
  44: migrate those two collections now.** Neither Socialite holder has actually triggered the collision
  45: yet (`office_merit_dots` currently holds Enforcer and Head of State only — single-seat offices,
  46: unaffected). Migrating two collections nobody has hit a real bug in yet, speculatively, is exactly
  47: the kind of unscoped work this project's stories consistently avoid. Record the gap explicitly (see
  48: Task 4) and revisit if/when an ST actually tries to set dots for a specific Socialite (or other
  49: multi-seat) holder.
  50: 
  51: **Finding 4 — `OFFICE_DATA` is still a static JS module**, three live import sites. The epic's own
  52: oxp.1 text bundles "migrate OFFICE_DATA off static JS" into this story. **This story splits that out
  53: into a new follow-up, `oxp-10-office-data-mongo-migration`** (added to `sprint-status.yaml` as
  54: `backlog` by this story's own creation). Reasoning: this is a separate, mechanical migration
  55: (move a static object into Mongo, build read/write plumbing, repoint three import sites) with its
  56: own risk surface, unrelated to the seat-schema/creation-date problem this story actually needs to
  57: solve. Bundling both into one story risks exactly the oversized-story pattern this project's own
  58: conventions warn against (see `specs/project-context.md`, and compare to how issue-1143 was
  59: deliberately spun out of otc.2's review as its own story rather than absorbed).
  60: 
  61: ## What this story is NOT
  62: 
  63: - NOT Epic OXP's derived-XP calculation (oxp.2) — this story stores creation dates and seat
  64:   identity; deriving "months since creation minus spend" from them is oxp.2's job.
  65: - NOT handover logic (oxp.5) — this story does not add reset-on-handover behaviour for anything.
  66:   `office_seats` records who holds a seat NOW; detecting and reacting to a CHANGE of holder is out
  67:   of scope here.
  68: - NOT a migration of `office_merit_dots`/`office_manoeuvre_rank` to seat-keying (Finding 3 above) —
  69:   explicitly deferred, not silently dropped.
  70: - NOT `OFFICE_DATA`'s migration off static JS (Finding 4 above) — split to `oxp-10`.
  71: - NOT a new API route or any UI consumption of `office_seats`. This story delivers the collection,
  72:   its schema, and a seed migration proving the corrected real data is right — nothing reads it yet.
  73:   The first story that actually needs to READ `office_seats` (most likely oxp.2) builds whatever
  74:   route it needs then, shaped by its own real requirements rather than a route built speculatively
  75:   here with no consumer.
  76: - NOT a resolution of exactly when René St. Dominique's Primogen seat was created. The epic's
  77:   existing six known dates cover one Primogen seat only. This story's seed script must be built so
  78:   Angelus can supply the second Primogen seat's real creation date when the script is actually run —
  79:   do not guess or default it (e.g. to Game 1's date, which may or may not be correct — nobody has
  80:   confirmed it).
  81: 
  82: ## Acceptance Criteria
  83: 
  84: 1. A new MongoDB collection, `office_seats`, has an AJV schema file
  85:    (`server/schemas/office_seat.schema.js`, mirroring this project's existing schema-file
  86:    conventions — see `server/schemas/office_action.schema.js` for the shape/style to match) defining
  87:    one document per SEAT: `{ office_category, holder_id (nullable ObjectId ref to characters._id),
  88:    created_at (ISO date string), seat_label (nullable string, for a case like Socialite's two seats
  89:    needing a human-readable distinguisher beyond office_category alone — e.g. "Appointed Harpy" /
  90:    "Popular Harpy"), notes (nullable string, free text) }`. `office_category` is validated against
  91:    the same five values `OFFICE_DATA`/`character.schema.js`'s `court_category` enum uses. No field
  92:    assumes exactly one seat per office — the schema must support an arbitrary number of documents
  93:    sharing the same `office_category`.
  94: 2. The collection does NOT key on `character.court_category` as its own identity — a seat's identity
  95:    is its own document `_id` (a real MongoDB ObjectId), independent of who currently holds it or
  96:    what that holder's `court_category` string says. `holder_id` is the seat's current pointer to a
  97:    character, nullable (a seat can be vacant), and typed consistently as an ObjectId (never a mixed
  98:    string/ObjectId — Known Drift Pattern #2 in `data-map.md` applies directly here).
  99: 3. A migration/seed script (`server/scripts/seed-office-seats.mjs` or equivalent, matching this
 100:    project's existing `server/scripts/` naming conventions) creates one `office_seats` document for
 101:    each of the seven real, currently-held seats confirmed live during this story's own data-lock:
 102:    Head of State (Eve Lockridge), Primogen × 2 (Yusuf Kalusicj, René St. Dominique — see the "What
 103:    this story is NOT" note on René's creation date), Enforcer (Einar Solveig), Socialite × 2 (Brandy
 104:    LaRoux "Harpy", Carver "People's Harpy"), Administrator (Ivana Horvat). Each seat's `holder_id`
 105:    points at the real character ObjectId. The script must be idempotent (safe to re-run without
 106:    duplicating documents — upsert on a natural key such as `{office_category, holder_id}`, or check
 107:    for an existing seat before inserting) and must NOT run automatically on server boot or in test
 108:    setup; it is a deliberate, manually-invoked ST-side operation, the same posture as this project's
 109:    other one-off `server/scripts/` migration scripts.
 110: 4. A test file (`server/tests/oxp-1-office-seats.test.js`) proves: the schema accepts a valid seat
 111:    document and rejects an invalid `office_category`; a vacant seat (`holder_id: null`) is valid;
 112:    two documents with the same `office_category` but different `holder_id` are both valid
 113:    simultaneously (the structural proof that N-per-office is really supported, not just claimed);
 114:    and — if practical against a real or seeded test-DB state — that the seed script's expected seven
 115:    documents exist with the right `office_category`/`holder_id` pairing after running it. DB-backed
 116:    tests follow this project's `describe.skipIf(!dbAvailable)` convention.
 117: 5. This story's Dev Notes record, explicitly and in the story's own words (not just a citation), the
 118:    three deliberate scope exclusions from Finding 3, Finding 4, and the René-date gap — so a future
 119:    reader of `sprint-status.yaml`'s oxp.1 entry understands these are decisions, not oversights.
 120: 6. `sprint-status.yaml` gains a new entry, `oxp-10-office-data-mongo-migration: backlog`, with a
 121:    comment explaining it was split out of oxp.1 during this story's own creation and why (Finding 4).

+# Adversarial review — oxp-1
+
+## High
+
+- **[Pass 1] The purported ISO-date guard accepts impossible dates and malformed timestamps.** Severity: High. File: `server/schemas/office_seat.schema.js:76`; mirrored in `server/scripts/seed-office-seats.mjs:109`. Trigger: supply Rene's required override as `2026-99-99` (or a syntactically matching timestamp such as `2026-02-21T+++`). Observable consequence: `buildSeatDocs` accepts the value and an `--apply` run can persist it to the live collection even though downstream date arithmetic can produce `NaN`, exactly the silent bad-XP outcome the guard says it prevents; the schema accepts the same bad value. The tests cover prose (`21 February 2026`) but no calendar-invalid matching value. Confidence: High (direct regex analysis; no script or database invocation).
+
+## Medium
+
+- **[Pass 1] The seed is only sequentially idempotent; concurrent applies can insert duplicate natural keys.** Severity: Medium. File: `server/scripts/seed-office-seats.mjs:167-189`. Trigger: two `seedOfficeSeats(..., { apply: true })` calls overlap so both `findOne({ office_category, holder_id })` operations for a seat finish before either `insertOne`. Observable consequence: both calls insert a document for the same purported natural key because the diff adds neither an atomic upsert nor a unique compound index. The only idempotency test calls the function twice sequentially, so the unqualified doc-comment claim “Idempotent by the natural key” and the rerun guidance do not cover this race. Confidence: High (direct control-flow analysis).
+
+## Low
+
+- **[Pass 1] Bare invocation establishes a live connection before rejecting the missing Rene date.** Severity: Low. File: `server/scripts/seed-office-seats.mjs:204-230`. Trigger: invoke the script with zero flags in the documented `server/.env` environment. Observable consequence: argument parsing selects dry-run and a null Rene date, but `main` calls `connectDb()` before `seedOfficeSeats` calls `buildSeatDocs` and throws; this makes no collection query or write, but does contact live Atlas, so the strongest safe failure would validate arguments before connecting and the “dry-run default is what makes that safe” wording omits the avoidable live connection. Confidence: High (direct control-flow analysis; invocation was forbidden and not attempted).
+
+- **[Pass 1] The “second validator” precaution neither creates a second validator nor is needed for these assertions.** Severity: Low. File: `server/tests/oxp-1-office-seats.test.js:193-221`. Trigger: run any N-seats-per-office schema test. Observable consequence: `ajv.compile(officeSeatSchema)` on the same schema object is cached by AJV and can return the same validation function; moreover each assertion evaluates its validation result and `.errors` message before the next validation call, so no later call can overwrite the earlier assertion's message. The tests still prove both individual documents validate, but the comments overstate a simultaneous-validation safeguard and do not themselves prove collection coexistence (the later DB tests do when they run). Confidence: Medium-High (AJV caching semantics plus JavaScript argument evaluation; repository/AJV version not yet opened in this pass).
+
+- **[Pass 1] The stored-document round-trip test only validates a hand-stringified surrogate.** Severity: Low. File: `server/schemas/office_seat.schema.js:86`; `server/tests/oxp-1-office-seats.test.js:101-105,375-379`. Trigger: pass a raw MongoDB document, whose `_id` and non-null `holder_id` are BSON `ObjectId` instances, directly to the schema validator. Observable consequence: both fields fail the schema's string typing; the DB-backed test avoids this by explicitly converting both values with `String(...)`, and the nominal round-trip test constructs `_id` as a string from the outset. That may be the intended JSON boundary, but the diff contains no consumer establishing it, so the test title does not prove a raw stored document round-trips. Confidence: High about the mismatch; Medium about impact because the diff intentionally adds no consumer.
+

 197: ### Current state of relevant files
 198: 
 199: **`character.schema.js:78`**: `court_category` is a plain nullable enum string — no seat-instance
 200: concept, confirmed both by direct schema reading and by oxp.4's own independent investigation (its
 201: story file). This story's `office_seats` collection is additive — it does not replace or modify
 202: `court_category` in any way; a character's `court_category` and their `office_seats` document(s) are
 203: two separate, currently-unlinked facts that happen to usually agree. (Whether they should be
 204: formally linked — e.g. `court_category` derived FROM holding a seat, rather than an independent
 205: field two write paths could disagree about — is a real future design question, out of scope here;
 206: noting it so it isn't lost.)
 207: 
 208: **`server/routes/office-merit-dots.js`, `server/routes/office-manoeuvre-rank.js`**: both keyed by
 209: `office_category` string only (`_id: category`). Untouched by this story (Finding 3). Their own
 210: comments already cite `oxp.4`'s handover-persistence reasoning; a future story that DOES migrate
 211: them to seat-keying should read both files' existing comments first, since they document the exact
 212: current keying this story's `office_seats` collection does not yet connect to.
 213: 
 214: **`public/js/tabs/office-data.js`**: unchanged by this story (Finding 4, split to `oxp-10`).
 215: 
 216: ### Deliberate scope exclusions (AC5) — decisions, not oversights
 217: 
 218: Three things a reader of `sprint-status.yaml`'s oxp.1 entry might reasonably expect to find in this
 219: story's diff, and deliberately will not. Each was decided before implementation, and none is a
 220: "ran out of time".
 221: 
 222: **1. `office_merit_dots` and `office_manoeuvre_rank` are NOT migrated to seat-keying.** Both
 223: collections key on the office category string alone (`_id: 'Socialite'`), which oxp.3 and oxp.4 both
 224: justified at the time on the grounds that there was no seat-ambiguity problem to solve. That
 225: reasoning is now demonstrably wrong: Socialite has two live seats, so the moment either Brandy
 226: LaRoux or Carver gets a real merit or manoeuvre-rank purchase, the two of them silently share one
 227: document and there is no way to tell whose purchase is whose. It has not happened yet.
 228: `office_merit_dots` currently holds Enforcer and Head of State only, both single-seat offices, and
 229: `office_manoeuvre_rank` is in the same position. Migrating two collections that nobody has hit a
 230: real bug in, speculatively, ahead of any consumer that would use the new keying, is precisely the
 231: unscoped work this project's stories avoid. The gap is recorded here rather than fixed; revisit it
 232: when an ST actually tries to set dots or a rank for one specific holder of a multi-seat office. The
 233: new `office_seats` collection is not wired to either of them in any direction.
 234: 
 235: **2. `OFFICE_DATA`'s static-JS-to-MongoDB migration is split out to `oxp-10`.** The epic's own
 236: oxp.1 text bundled it in here. It is a distinct, mechanical migration (lift a static object out of
 237: `public/js/tabs/office-data.js` into a collection, build the read/write plumbing, repoint three live
 238: import sites) whose risk surface is entirely unrelated to the seat-identity problem this story
 239: exists to solve. `specs/stories/sprint-status.yaml` line 983 carries the new `oxp-10` entry and the
 240: reason. `public/js/tabs/office-data.js` is untouched by this story's diff.
 241: 
 242: One thing implementation surfaced that the story's own drafting did not: `OFFICE_DATA` defines only
 243: **four** offices, not five. Administrator has no manoeuvre or merit content yet (that is oxp.8), so
 244: the module has no key for it, while `character.schema.js`'s `court_category` enum does. The
 245: Administrator seat is real and filled (Ivana Horvat, since Game 5) and had to be seeded, so
 246: `office_seat.schema.js`'s category enum follows `character.schema.js`, not `OFFICE_DATA`. AC1's
 247: phrasing treats the two as interchangeable sources for "the same five values"; they are not, and
 248: `oxp-10` will need to reconcile that when it moves `OFFICE_DATA` into Mongo. A test in
 249: `oxp-1-office-seats.test.js` asserts the enum stays in lockstep with `court_category` specifically,
 250: so a future edit to either one fails loudly.
 251: 
 252: **3. Rene St. Dominique's Primogen seat creation date is still unknown, by design.** This is an open
 253: DATA question for whoever runs the seed script, not a design gap in the schema, which stores
 254: whatever date it is given. The epic's six known dates cover one Primogen seat, and which of the two
 255: live Primogen it describes has never been established. The seed script therefore refuses to build
 256: its documents at all unless the date arrives via `--rene-created-at=YYYY-MM-DD` or the
 257: `RENE_PRIMOGEN_SEAT_CREATED_AT` constant, and rejects a non-ISO value rather than storing rubbish.
 258: It is not defaulted to Game 1's `2026-02-21`; that would look right and could be silently wrong, and
 259: oxp.2's months-since-creation arithmetic would then produce a wrong XP figure in a place nobody

+# Adversarial review — oxp-1
+
+## High
+
+- **[Pass 1] The purported ISO-date guard accepts impossible dates and malformed timestamps.** Severity: High. File: `server/schemas/office_seat.schema.js:76`; mirrored in `server/scripts/seed-office-seats.mjs:109`. Trigger: supply Rene's required override as `2026-99-99` (or a syntactically matching timestamp such as `2026-02-21T+++`). Observable consequence: `buildSeatDocs` accepts the value and an `--apply` run can persist it to the live collection even though downstream date arithmetic can produce `NaN`, exactly the silent bad-XP outcome the guard says it prevents; the schema accepts the same bad value. The tests cover prose (`21 February 2026`) but no calendar-invalid matching value. Confidence: High (direct regex analysis; no script or database invocation).
+
+## Medium
+
+- **[Pass 1] The seed is only sequentially idempotent; concurrent applies can insert duplicate natural keys.** Severity: Medium. File: `server/scripts/seed-office-seats.mjs:167-189`. Trigger: two `seedOfficeSeats(..., { apply: true })` calls overlap so both `findOne({ office_category, holder_id })` operations for a seat finish before either `insertOne`. Observable consequence: both calls insert a document for the same purported natural key because the diff adds neither an atomic upsert nor a unique compound index. The only idempotency test calls the function twice sequentially, so the unqualified doc-comment claim “Idempotent by the natural key” and the rerun guidance do not cover this race. Confidence: High (direct control-flow analysis).
+
+## Low
+
+- **[Pass 1] Bare invocation establishes a live connection before rejecting the missing Rene date.** Severity: Low. File: `server/scripts/seed-office-seats.mjs:204-230`. Trigger: invoke the script with zero flags in the documented `server/.env` environment. Observable consequence: argument parsing selects dry-run and a null Rene date, but `main` calls `connectDb()` before `seedOfficeSeats` calls `buildSeatDocs` and throws; this makes no collection query or write, but does contact live Atlas, so the strongest safe failure would validate arguments before connecting and the “dry-run default is what makes that safe” wording omits the avoidable live connection. Confidence: High (direct control-flow analysis; invocation was forbidden and not attempted).
+
+- **[Pass 1] The “second validator” precaution neither creates a second validator nor is needed for these assertions.** Severity: Low. File: `server/tests/oxp-1-office-seats.test.js:193-221`. Trigger: run any N-seats-per-office schema test. Observable consequence: `ajv.compile(officeSeatSchema)` on the same schema object is cached by AJV and can return the same validation function; moreover each assertion evaluates its validation result and `.errors` message before the next validation call, so no later call can overwrite the earlier assertion's message. The tests still prove both individual documents validate, but the comments overstate a simultaneous-validation safeguard and do not themselves prove collection coexistence (the later DB tests do when they run). Confidence: Medium-High (AJV caching semantics plus JavaScript argument evaluation; repository/AJV version not yet opened in this pass).
+
+- **[Pass 1] The stored-document round-trip test only validates a hand-stringified surrogate.** Severity: Low. File: `server/schemas/office_seat.schema.js:86`; `server/tests/oxp-1-office-seats.test.js:101-105,375-379`. Trigger: pass a raw MongoDB document, whose `_id` and non-null `holder_id` are BSON `ObjectId` instances, directly to the schema validator. Observable consequence: both fields fail the schema's string typing; the DB-backed test avoids this by explicitly converting both values with `String(...)`, and the nominal round-trip test constructs `_id` as a string from the outset. That may be the intended JSON boundary, but the diff contains no consumer establishing it, so the test title does not prove a raw stored document round-trips. Confidence: High about the mismatch; Medium about impact because the diff intentionally adds no consumer.
+

+- **[Pass 1] The seed is only sequentially idempotent; concurrent applies can insert duplicate natural keys.** Severity: Medium. File: `server/scripts/seed-office-seats.mjs:167-189`. Trigger: two `seedOfficeSeats(..., { apply: true })` calls overlap so both `findOne({ office_category, holder_id })` operations for a seat finish before either `insertOne`. Observable consequence: both calls insert a document for the same purported natural key because the diff adds neither an atomic upsert nor a unique compound index. The only idempotency test calls the function twice sequentially, so the unqualified doc-comment claim “Idempotent by the natural key” and the rerun guidance do not cover this race. Confidence: High (direct control-flow analysis).
+
+## Low
+
+- **[Pass 1] Bare invocation establishes a live connection before rejecting the missing Rene date.** Severity: Low. File: `server/scripts/seed-office-seats.mjs:204-230`. Trigger: invoke the script with zero flags in the documented `server/.env` environment. Observable consequence: argument parsing selects dry-run and a null Rene date, but `main` calls `connectDb()` before `seedOfficeSeats` calls `buildSeatDocs` and throws; this makes no collection query or write, but does contact live Atlas, so the strongest safe failure would validate arguments before connecting and the “dry-run default is what makes that safe” wording omits the avoidable live connection. Confidence: High (direct control-flow analysis; invocation was forbidden and not attempted).
+
+- **[Pass 1] The “second validator” precaution neither creates a second validator nor is needed for these assertions.** Severity: Low. File: `server/tests/oxp-1-office-seats.test.js:193-221`. Trigger: run any N-seats-per-office schema test. Observable consequence: `ajv.compile(officeSeatSchema)` on the same schema object is cached by AJV and can return the same validation function; moreover each assertion evaluates its validation result and `.errors` message before the next validation call, so no later call can overwrite the earlier assertion's message. The tests still prove both individual documents validate, but the comments overstate a simultaneous-validation safeguard and do not themselves prove collection coexistence (the later DB tests do when they run). Confidence: Medium-High (AJV caching semantics plus JavaScript argument evaluation; repository/AJV version not yet opened in this pass).
+
+- **[Pass 1] The stored-document round-trip test only validates a hand-stringified surrogate.** Severity: Low. File: `server/schemas/office_seat.schema.js:86`; `server/tests/oxp-1-office-seats.test.js:101-105,375-379`. Trigger: pass a raw MongoDB document, whose `_id` and non-null `holder_id` are BSON `ObjectId` instances, directly to the schema validator. Observable consequence: both fields fail the schema's string typing; the DB-backed test avoids this by explicitly converting both values with `String(...)`, and the nominal round-trip test constructs `_id` as a string from the outset. That may be the intended JSON boundary, but the diff contains no consumer establishing it, so the test title does not prove a raw stored document round-trips. Confidence: High about the mismatch; Medium about impact because the diff intentionally adds no consumer.

+# Adversarial review — oxp-1
+
+## High
+
+- **[Pass 1] The purported ISO-date guard accepts impossible dates and malformed timestamps.** Severity: High. File: `server/schemas/office_seat.schema.js:76`; mirrored in `server/scripts/seed-office-seats.mjs:109`. Trigger: supply Rene's required override as `2026-99-99` (or a syntactically matching timestamp such as `2026-02-21T+++`). Observable consequence: `buildSeatDocs` accepts the value and an `--apply` run can persist it to the live collection even though downstream date arithmetic can produce `NaN`, exactly the silent bad-XP outcome the guard says it prevents; the schema accepts the same bad value. The tests cover prose (`21 February 2026`) but no calendar-invalid matching value. Confidence: High (direct regex analysis; no script or database invocation).
+
+## Medium
+
+- **[Pass 1] The seed is only sequentially idempotent; concurrent applies can insert duplicate natural keys.** Severity: Medium. File: `server/scripts/seed-office-seats.mjs:167-189`. Trigger: two `seedOfficeSeats(..., { apply: true })` calls overlap so both `findOne({ office_category, holder_id })` operations for a seat finish before either `insertOne`. Observable consequence: both calls insert a document for the same purported natural key because the diff adds neither an atomic upsert nor a unique compound index. The only idempotency test calls the function twice sequentially, so the unqualified doc-comment claim “Idempotent by the natural key” and the rerun guidance do not cover this race. Confidence: High (direct control-flow analysis).
+
+## Low
+
+- **[Pass 1] Bare invocation establishes a live connection before rejecting the missing Rene date.** Severity: Low. File: `server/scripts/seed-office-seats.mjs:204-230`. Trigger: invoke the script with zero flags in the documented `server/.env` environment. Observable consequence: argument parsing selects dry-run and a null Rene date, but `main` calls `connectDb()` before `seedOfficeSeats` calls `buildSeatDocs` and throws; this makes no collection query or write, but does contact live Atlas, so the strongest safe failure would validate arguments before connecting and the “dry-run default is what makes that safe” wording omits the avoidable live connection. Confidence: High (direct control-flow analysis; invocation was forbidden and not attempted).
+
+- **[Pass 1] The “second validator” precaution neither creates a second validator nor is needed for these assertions.** Severity: Low. File: `server/tests/oxp-1-office-seats.test.js:193-221`. Trigger: run any N-seats-per-office schema test. Observable consequence: `ajv.compile(officeSeatSchema)` on the same schema object is cached by AJV and can return the same validation function; moreover each assertion evaluates its validation result and `.errors` message before the next validation call, so no later call can overwrite the earlier assertion's message. The tests still prove both individual documents validate, but the comments overstate a simultaneous-validation safeguard and do not themselves prove collection coexistence (the later DB tests do when they run). Confidence: Medium-High (AJV caching semantics plus JavaScript argument evaluation; repository/AJV version not yet opened in this pass).
+
+- **[Pass 1] The stored-document round-trip test only validates a hand-stringified surrogate.** Severity: Low. File: `server/schemas/office_seat.schema.js:86`; `server/tests/oxp-1-office-seats.test.js:101-105,375-379`. Trigger: pass a raw MongoDB document, whose `_id` and non-null `holder_id` are BSON `ObjectId` instances, directly to the schema validator. Observable consequence: both fields fail the schema's string typing; the DB-backed test avoids this by explicitly converting both values with `String(...)`, and the nominal round-trip test constructs `_id` as a string from the outset. That may be the intended JSON boundary, but the diff contains no consumer establishing it, so the test title does not prove a raw stored document round-trips. Confidence: High about the mismatch; Medium about impact because the diff intentionally adds no consumer.
+
+- **[Pass 3a] AC1 is literally unsatisfiable as written because its two named enum sources do not share five values.** Severity: Low. File: `specs/stories/oxp-1-data-lock-office-seat-schema.md:84-93`; `server/schemas/office_seat.schema.js:45-56`. Trigger: audit the implementation against AC1's statement that the same five values are used by both `OFFICE_DATA` and `character.schema.js`. Observable consequence: `OFFICE_DATA` has only four categories and lacks `Administrator`, while the character schema has five; the implementation sensibly follows the character schema and the story's Dev Notes explicitly explain this, but AC1 was not corrected, so literal full-AC conformance cannot be truthfully claimed. Confidence: High (direct source comparison; this is specification debt, not a recommendation to remove Administrator).

 381:   compile time. That constraint is real and is respected, but a bare string was rejected here on the
 382:   grounds that these dates feed oxp.2's months-since-creation arithmetic: `'21 February 2026'`
 383:   parses to `NaN` there and yields a silently wrong XP figure rather than a loud failure. The
 384:   pattern is deliberately permissive about time (`'2026-02-21'` and `'2026-02-21T09:30:00.000Z'`
 385:   both pass) and strict only about the leading `YYYY-MM-DD`.
 386: 
 387: - **The seed script takes its collection as an argument.** `seedOfficeSeats(collection, opts)` never
 388:   resolves a collection itself; only `main()` does, and `main()` runs only under the direct-invoke
 389:   guard (`import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href`, the `backfill-free-grants.js`
 390:   pattern). That is what lets the tests exercise the real seeding logic end to end while making it
 391:   structurally impossible for an import to reach live Atlas.
 392: 
 393: - **Idempotency skips rather than upserts, on purpose.** AC3 permits either. An existing seat for a
 394:   `{office_category, holder_id}` pair is left completely alone, including any `notes` or
 395:   `seat_label` an ST has hand-edited since seeding, which an upsert would silently overwrite back to
 396:   the hardcoded table's values. A test covers exactly that ST-edit-survives-re-run case, and another
 397:   covers the partial-state case (delete one seat, re-run, one insert, the other six keep their
 398:   original `_id`s so seat identity stays stable).
 399: 
 400: - **Dry-run is the default and `--apply` is required to write**, matching
 401:   `seed-rules-pool-grants.js` and `backfill-free-grants.js`. Since the script resolves its
 402:   connection through `../db.js`, running it bare from `server/` with `server/.env` in place targets
 403:   live Atlas; the dry-run default is what makes that survivable, and the script's header says so
 404:   in as many words.

 407:   under "Deliberate scope exclusions" above, with the consequence for `oxp-10`. The category enum

+# Adversarial review — oxp-1
+
+## High
+
+- **[Pass 1] The purported ISO-date guard accepts impossible dates and malformed timestamps.** Severity: High. File: `server/schemas/office_seat.schema.js:76`; mirrored in `server/scripts/seed-office-seats.mjs:109`. Trigger: supply Rene's required override as `2026-99-99` (or a syntactically matching timestamp such as `2026-02-21T+++`). Observable consequence: `buildSeatDocs` accepts the value and an `--apply` run can persist it to the live collection even though downstream date arithmetic can produce `NaN`, exactly the silent bad-XP outcome the guard says it prevents; the schema accepts the same bad value. The tests cover prose (`21 February 2026`) but no calendar-invalid matching value. Confidence: High (direct regex analysis; no script or database invocation).
+
+## Medium
+
+- **[Pass 1] The seed is only sequentially idempotent; concurrent applies can insert duplicate natural keys.** Severity: Medium. File: `server/scripts/seed-office-seats.mjs:167-189`. Trigger: two `seedOfficeSeats(..., { apply: true })` calls overlap so both `findOne({ office_category, holder_id })` operations for a seat finish before either `insertOne`. Observable consequence: both calls insert a document for the same purported natural key because the diff adds neither an atomic upsert nor a unique compound index. The only idempotency test calls the function twice sequentially, so the unqualified doc-comment claim “Idempotent by the natural key” and the rerun guidance do not cover this race. Confidence: High (direct control-flow analysis).
+
+## Low
+
+- **[Pass 1] Bare invocation establishes a live connection before rejecting the missing Rene date.** Severity: Low. File: `server/scripts/seed-office-seats.mjs:204-230`. Trigger: invoke the script with zero flags in the documented `server/.env` environment. Observable consequence: argument parsing selects dry-run and a null Rene date, but `main` calls `connectDb()` before `seedOfficeSeats` calls `buildSeatDocs` and throws; this makes no collection query or write, but does contact live Atlas, so the strongest safe failure would validate arguments before connecting and the “dry-run default is what makes that safe” wording omits the avoidable live connection. Confidence: High (direct control-flow analysis; invocation was forbidden and not attempted).
+
+- **[Pass 1] The “second validator” precaution neither creates a second validator nor is needed for these assertions.** Severity: Low. File: `server/tests/oxp-1-office-seats.test.js:193-221`. Trigger: run any N-seats-per-office schema test. Observable consequence: `ajv.compile(officeSeatSchema)` on the same schema object is cached by AJV and can return the same validation function; moreover each assertion evaluates its validation result and `.errors` message before the next validation call, so no later call can overwrite the earlier assertion's message. The tests still prove both individual documents validate, but the comments overstate a simultaneous-validation safeguard and do not themselves prove collection coexistence (the later DB tests do when they run). Confidence: Medium-High (AJV caching semantics plus JavaScript argument evaluation; repository/AJV version not yet opened in this pass).
+
+- **[Pass 1] The stored-document round-trip test only validates a hand-stringified surrogate.** Severity: Low. File: `server/schemas/office_seat.schema.js:86`; `server/tests/oxp-1-office-seats.test.js:101-105,375-379`. Trigger: pass a raw MongoDB document, whose `_id` and non-null `holder_id` are BSON `ObjectId` instances, directly to the schema validator. Observable consequence: both fields fail the schema's string typing; the DB-backed test avoids this by explicitly converting both values with `String(...)`, and the nominal round-trip test constructs `_id` as a string from the outset. That may be the intended JSON boundary, but the diff contains no consumer establishing it, so the test title does not prove a raw stored document round-trips. Confidence: High about the mismatch; Medium about impact because the diff intentionally adds no consumer.
+
+- **[Pass 3a] AC1 is literally unsatisfiable as written because its two named enum sources do not share five values.** Severity: Low. File: `specs/stories/oxp-1-data-lock-office-seat-schema.md:84-93`; `server/schemas/office_seat.schema.js:45-56`. Trigger: audit the implementation against AC1's statement that the same five values are used by both `OFFICE_DATA` and `character.schema.js`. Observable consequence: `OFFICE_DATA` has only four categories and lacks `Administrator`, while the character schema has five; the implementation sensibly follows the character schema and the story's Dev Notes explicitly explain this, but AC1 was not corrected, so literal full-AC conformance cannot be truthfully claimed. Confidence: High (direct source comparison; this is specification debt, not a recommendation to remove Administrator).
