+- **[Pass 1] The purported ISO-date guard accepts impossible dates and malformed timestamps.** Severity: High. File: `server/schemas/office_seat.schema.js:76`; mirrored in `server/scripts/seed-office-seats.mjs:109`. Trigger: supply Rene's required override as `2026-99-99` (or a syntactically matching timestamp such as `2026-02-21T+++`). Observable consequence: `buildSeatDocs` accepts the value and an `--apply` run can persist it to the live collection even though downstream date arithmetic can produce `NaN`, exactly the silent bad-XP outcome the guard says it prevents; the schema accepts the same bad value. The tests cover prose (`21 February 2026`) but no calendar-invalid matching value. Confidence: High (direct regex analysis; no script or database invocation).
+
+## Medium
+
+- **[Pass 1] The seed is only sequentially idempotent; concurrent applies can insert duplicate natural keys.** Severity: Medium. File: `server/scripts/seed-office-seats.mjs:167-189`. Trigger: two `seedOfficeSeats(..., { apply: true })` calls overlap so both `findOne({ office_category, holder_id })` operations for a seat finish before either `insertOne`. Observable consequence: both calls insert a document for the same purported natural key because the diff adds neither an atomic upsert nor a unique compound index. The only idempotency test calls the function twice sequentially, so the unqualified doc-comment claim “Idempotent by the natural key” and the rerun guidance do not cover this race. Confidence: High (direct control-flow analysis).
+
+## Low
+
+- **[Pass 1] Bare invocation establishes a live connection before rejecting the missing Rene date.** Severity: Low. File: `server/scripts/seed-office-seats.mjs:204-230`. Trigger: invoke the script with zero flags in the documented `server/.env` environment. Observable consequence: argument parsing selects dry-run and a null Rene date, but `main` calls `connectDb()` before `seedOfficeSeats` calls `buildSeatDocs` and throws; this makes no collection query or write, but does contact live Atlas, so the strongest safe failure would validate arguments before connecting and the “dry-run default is what makes that safe” wording omits the avoidable live connection. Confidence: High (direct control-flow analysis; invocation was forbidden and not attempted).
+
+- **[Pass 1] The “second validator” precaution neither creates a second validator nor is needed for these assertions.** Severity: Low. File: `server/tests/oxp-1-office-seats.test.js:193-221`. Trigger: run any N-seats-per-office schema test. Observable consequence: `ajv.compile(officeSeatSchema)` on the same schema object is cached by AJV and can return the same validation function; moreover each assertion evaluates its validation result and `.errors` message before the next validation call, so no later call can overwrite the earlier assertion's message. The tests still prove both individual documents validate, but the comments overstate a simultaneous-validation safeguard and do not themselves prove collection coexistence (the later DB tests do when they run). Confidence: Medium-High (AJV caching semantics plus JavaScript argument evaluation; repository/AJV version not yet opened in this pass).
+
+- **[Pass 1] The stored-document round-trip test only validates a hand-stringified surrogate.** Severity: Low. File: `server/schemas/office_seat.schema.js:86`; `server/tests/oxp-1-office-seats.test.js:101-105,375-379`. Trigger: pass a raw MongoDB document, whose `_id` and non-null `holder_id` are BSON `ObjectId` instances, directly to the schema validator. Observable consequence: both fields fail the schema's string typing; the DB-backed test avoids this by explicitly converting both values with `String(...)`, and the nominal round-trip test constructs `_id` as a string from the outset. That may be the intended JSON boundary, but the diff contains no consumer establishing it, so the test title does not prove a raw stored document round-trips. Confidence: High about the mismatch; Medium about impact because the diff intentionally adds no consumer.
+
+- **[Pass 3a] AC1 is literally unsatisfiable as written because its two named enum sources do not share five values.** Severity: Low. File: `specs/stories/oxp-1-data-lock-office-seat-schema.md:84-93`; `server/schemas/office_seat.schema.js:45-56`. Trigger: audit the implementation against AC1's statement that the same five values are used by both `OFFICE_DATA` and `character.schema.js`. Observable consequence: `OFFICE_DATA` has only four categories and lacks `Administrator`, while the character schema has five; the implementation sensibly follows the character schema and the story's Dev Notes explicitly explain this, but AC1 was not corrected, so literal full-AC conformance cannot be truthfully claimed. Confidence: High (direct source comparison; this is specification debt, not a recommendation to remove Administrator).

+# Adversarial review — oxp-1
+
+## High
+
+- **[Pass 1] The purported ISO-date guard accepts impossible dates and malformed timestamps.** Severity: High. File: `server/schemas/office_seat.schema.js:76`; mirrored in `server/scripts/seed-office-seats.mjs:109`. Trigger: supply Rene's required override as `2026-99-99` (or a syntactically matching timestamp such as `2026-02-21T+++`). Observable consequence: `buildSeatDocs` accepts the value and an `--apply` run can persist it to the live collection even though downstream date arithmetic can produce `NaN`, exactly the silent bad-XP outcome the guard says it prevents; the schema accepts the same bad value. The tests cover prose (`21 February 2026`) but no calendar-invalid matching value. Confidence: High (direct regex analysis; no script or database invocation).
+
+## Medium
+
+- **[Pass 1] The seed is only sequentially idempotent; concurrent applies can insert duplicate natural keys.** Severity: Medium. File: `server/scripts/seed-office-seats.mjs:167-189`. Trigger: two `seedOfficeSeats(..., { apply: true })` calls overlap so both `findOne({ office_category, holder_id })` operations for a seat finish before either `insertOne`. Observable consequence: both calls insert a document for the same purported natural key because the diff adds neither an atomic upsert nor a unique compound index. The only idempotency test calls the function twice sequentially, so the unqualified doc-comment claim “Idempotent by the natural key” and the rerun guidance do not cover this race. Confidence: High (direct control-flow analysis).
+
+## Low
+
+- **[Pass 1] Bare invocation establishes a live connection before rejecting the missing Rene date.** Severity: Low. File: `server/scripts/seed-office-seats.mjs:204-230`. Trigger: invoke the script with zero flags in the documented `server/.env` environment. Observable consequence: argument parsing selects dry-run and a null Rene date, but `main` calls `connectDb()` before `seedOfficeSeats` calls `buildSeatDocs` and throws; this makes no collection query or write, but does contact live Atlas, so the strongest safe failure would validate arguments before connecting and the “dry-run default is what makes that safe” wording omits the avoidable live connection. Confidence: High (direct control-flow analysis; invocation was forbidden and not attempted).
+
+- **[Pass 1] The “second validator” precaution neither creates a second validator nor is needed for these assertions.** Severity: Low. File: `server/tests/oxp-1-office-seats.test.js:193-221`. Trigger: run any N-seats-per-office schema test. Observable consequence: `ajv.compile(officeSeatSchema)` on the same schema object is cached by AJV and can return the same validation function; moreover each assertion evaluates its validation result and `.errors` message before the next validation call, so no later call can overwrite the earlier assertion's message. The tests still prove both individual documents validate, but the comments overstate a simultaneous-validation safeguard and do not themselves prove collection coexistence (the later DB tests do when they run). Confidence: Medium-High (AJV caching semantics plus JavaScript argument evaluation; repository/AJV version not yet opened in this pass).
+
+- **[Pass 1] The stored-document round-trip test only validates a hand-stringified surrogate.** Severity: Low. File: `server/schemas/office_seat.schema.js:86`; `server/tests/oxp-1-office-seats.test.js:101-105,375-379`. Trigger: pass a raw MongoDB document, whose `_id` and non-null `holder_id` are BSON `ObjectId` instances, directly to the schema validator. Observable consequence: both fields fail the schema's string typing; the DB-backed test avoids this by explicitly converting both values with `String(...)`, and the nominal round-trip test constructs `_id` as a string from the outset. That may be the intended JSON boundary, but the diff contains no consumer establishing it, so the test title does not prove a raw stored document round-trips. Confidence: High about the mismatch; Medium about impact because the diff intentionally adds no consumer.
+
+- **[Pass 3a] AC1 is literally unsatisfiable as written because its two named enum sources do not share five values.** Severity: Low. File: `specs/stories/oxp-1-data-lock-office-seat-schema.md:84-93`; `server/schemas/office_seat.schema.js:45-56`. Trigger: audit the implementation against AC1's statement that the same five values are used by both `OFFICE_DATA` and `character.schema.js`. Observable consequence: `OFFICE_DATA` has only four categories and lacks `Administrator`, while the character schema has five; the implementation sensibly follows the character schema and the story's Dev Notes explicitly explain this, but AC1 was not corrected, so literal full-AC conformance cannot be truthfully claimed. Confidence: High (direct source comparison; this is specification debt, not a recommendation to remove Administrator).
+

+# Adversarial review — oxp-1
+
+## High
+
+- **[Pass 1] The purported ISO-date guard accepts impossible dates and malformed timestamps.** Severity: High. File: `server/schemas/office_seat.schema.js:76`; mirrored in `server/scripts/seed-office-seats.mjs:109`. Trigger: supply Rene's required override as `2026-99-99` (or a syntactically matching timestamp such as `2026-02-21T+++`). Observable consequence: `buildSeatDocs` accepts the value and an `--apply` run can persist it to the live collection even though downstream date arithmetic can produce `NaN`, exactly the silent bad-XP outcome the guard says it prevents; the schema accepts the same bad value. The tests cover prose (`21 February 2026`) but no calendar-invalid matching value. Confidence: High (direct regex analysis; no script or database invocation).
+
+## Medium
+
+- **[Pass 1] The seed is only sequentially idempotent; concurrent applies can insert duplicate natural keys.** Severity: Medium. File: `server/scripts/seed-office-seats.mjs:167-189`. Trigger: two `seedOfficeSeats(..., { apply: true })` calls overlap so both `findOne({ office_category, holder_id })` operations for a seat finish before either `insertOne`. Observable consequence: both calls insert a document for the same purported natural key because the diff adds neither an atomic upsert nor a unique compound index. The only idempotency test calls the function twice sequentially, so the unqualified doc-comment claim “Idempotent by the natural key” and the rerun guidance do not cover this race. Confidence: High (direct control-flow analysis).
+
+## Low
+
+- **[Pass 1] Bare invocation establishes a live connection before rejecting the missing Rene date.** Severity: Low. File: `server/scripts/seed-office-seats.mjs:204-230`. Trigger: invoke the script with zero flags in the documented `server/.env` environment. Observable consequence: argument parsing selects dry-run and a null Rene date, but `main` calls `connectDb()` before `seedOfficeSeats` calls `buildSeatDocs` and throws; this makes no collection query or write, but does contact live Atlas, so the strongest safe failure would validate arguments before connecting and the “dry-run default is what makes that safe” wording omits the avoidable live connection. Confidence: High (direct control-flow analysis; invocation was forbidden and not attempted).
+
+- **[Pass 1] The “second validator” precaution neither creates a second validator nor is needed for these assertions.** Severity: Low. File: `server/tests/oxp-1-office-seats.test.js:193-221`. Trigger: run any N-seats-per-office schema test. Observable consequence: `ajv.compile(officeSeatSchema)` on the same schema object is cached by AJV and can return the same validation function; moreover each assertion evaluates its validation result and `.errors` message before the next validation call, so no later call can overwrite the earlier assertion's message. The tests still prove both individual documents validate, but the comments overstate a simultaneous-validation safeguard and do not themselves prove collection coexistence (the later DB tests do when they run). Confidence: Medium-High (AJV caching semantics plus JavaScript argument evaluation; repository/AJV version not yet opened in this pass).
+
+- **[Pass 1] The stored-document round-trip test only validates a hand-stringified surrogate.** Severity: Low. File: `server/schemas/office_seat.schema.js:86`; `server/tests/oxp-1-office-seats.test.js:101-105,375-379`. Trigger: pass a raw MongoDB document, whose `_id` and non-null `holder_id` are BSON `ObjectId` instances, directly to the schema validator. Observable consequence: both fields fail the schema's string typing; the DB-backed test avoids this by explicitly converting both values with `String(...)`, and the nominal round-trip test constructs `_id` as a string from the outset. That may be the intended JSON boundary, but the diff contains no consumer establishing it, so the test title does not prove a raw stored document round-trips. Confidence: High about the mismatch; Medium about impact because the diff intentionally adds no consumer.
+
+- **[Pass 3a] AC1 is literally unsatisfiable as written because its two named enum sources do not share five values.** Severity: Low. File: `specs/stories/oxp-1-data-lock-office-seat-schema.md:84-93`; `server/schemas/office_seat.schema.js:45-56`. Trigger: audit the implementation against AC1's statement that the same five values are used by both `OFFICE_DATA` and `character.schema.js`. Observable consequence: `OFFICE_DATA` has only four categories and lacks `Administrator`, while the character schema has five; the implementation sensibly follows the character schema and the story's Dev Notes explicitly explain this, but AC1 was not corrected, so literal full-AC conformance cannot be truthfully claimed. Confidence: High (direct source comparison; this is specification debt, not a recommendation to remove Administrator).

+# Adversarial review — oxp-1
+
+## High
+
+- **[Pass 1] The purported ISO-date guard accepts impossible dates and malformed timestamps.** Severity: High. File: `server/schemas/office_seat.schema.js:76`; mirrored in `server/scripts/seed-office-seats.mjs:109`. Trigger: supply Rene's required override as `2026-99-99` (or a syntactically matching timestamp such as `2026-02-21T+++`). Observable consequence: `buildSeatDocs` accepts the value and an `--apply` run can persist it to the live collection even though downstream date arithmetic can produce `NaN`, exactly the silent bad-XP outcome the guard says it prevents; the schema accepts the same bad value. The tests cover prose (`21 February 2026`) but no calendar-invalid matching value. Confidence: High (direct regex analysis; no script or database invocation).
+
+## Medium
+
+- **[Pass 1] The seed is only sequentially idempotent; concurrent applies can insert duplicate natural keys.** Severity: Medium. File: `server/scripts/seed-office-seats.mjs:167-189`. Trigger: two `seedOfficeSeats(..., { apply: true })` calls overlap so both `findOne({ office_category, holder_id })` operations for a seat finish before either `insertOne`. Observable consequence: both calls insert a document for the same purported natural key because the diff adds neither an atomic upsert nor a unique compound index. The only idempotency test calls the function twice sequentially, so the unqualified doc-comment claim “Idempotent by the natural key” and the rerun guidance do not cover this race. Confidence: High (direct control-flow analysis).
+
+## Low
+
+- **[Pass 1] Bare invocation establishes a live connection before rejecting the missing Rene date.** Severity: Low. File: `server/scripts/seed-office-seats.mjs:204-230`. Trigger: invoke the script with zero flags in the documented `server/.env` environment. Observable consequence: argument parsing selects dry-run and a null Rene date, but `main` calls `connectDb()` before `seedOfficeSeats` calls `buildSeatDocs` and throws; this makes no collection query or write, but does contact live Atlas, so the strongest safe failure would validate arguments before connecting and the “dry-run default is what makes that safe” wording omits the avoidable live connection. Confidence: High (direct control-flow analysis; invocation was forbidden and not attempted).
+
+- **[Pass 1] The “second validator” precaution neither creates a second validator nor is needed for these assertions.** Severity: Low. File: `server/tests/oxp-1-office-seats.test.js:193-221`. Trigger: run any N-seats-per-office schema test. Observable consequence: `ajv.compile(officeSeatSchema)` on the same schema object is cached by AJV and can return the same validation function; moreover each assertion evaluates its validation result and `.errors` message before the next validation call, so no later call can overwrite the earlier assertion's message. The tests still prove both individual documents validate, but the comments overstate a simultaneous-validation safeguard and do not themselves prove collection coexistence (the later DB tests do when they run). Confidence: Medium-High (AJV caching semantics plus JavaScript argument evaluation; repository/AJV version not yet opened in this pass).
+
+- **[Pass 1] The stored-document round-trip test only validates a hand-stringified surrogate.** Severity: Low. File: `server/schemas/office_seat.schema.js:86`; `server/tests/oxp-1-office-seats.test.js:101-105,375-379`. Trigger: pass a raw MongoDB document, whose `_id` and non-null `holder_id` are BSON `ObjectId` instances, directly to the schema validator. Observable consequence: both fields fail the schema's string typing; the DB-backed test avoids this by explicitly converting both values with `String(...)`, and the nominal round-trip test constructs `_id` as a string from the outset. That may be the intended JSON boundary, but the diff contains no consumer establishing it, so the test title does not prove a raw stored document round-trips. Confidence: High about the mismatch; Medium about impact because the diff intentionally adds no consumer.
+
+- **[Pass 3a] AC1 is literally unsatisfiable as written because its two named enum sources do not share five values.** Severity: Low. File: `specs/stories/oxp-1-data-lock-office-seat-schema.md:84-93`; `server/schemas/office_seat.schema.js:45-56`. Trigger: audit the implementation against AC1's statement that the same five values are used by both `OFFICE_DATA` and `character.schema.js`. Observable consequence: `OFFICE_DATA` has only four categories and lacks `Administrator`, while the character schema has five; the implementation sensibly follows the character schema and the story's Dev Notes explicitly explain this, but AC1 was not corrected, so literal full-AC conformance cannot be truthfully claimed. Confidence: High (direct source comparison; this is specification debt, not a recommendation to remove Administrator).

+# Adversarial review — oxp-1
+
+## High
+
+- **[Pass 1] The purported ISO-date guard accepts impossible dates and malformed timestamps.** Severity: High. File: `server/schemas/office_seat.schema.js:76`; mirrored in `server/scripts/seed-office-seats.mjs:109`. Trigger: supply Rene's required override as `2026-99-99` (or a syntactically matching timestamp such as `2026-02-21T+++`). Observable consequence: `buildSeatDocs` accepts the value and an `--apply` run can persist it to the live collection even though downstream date arithmetic can produce `NaN`, exactly the silent bad-XP outcome the guard says it prevents; the schema accepts the same bad value. The tests cover prose (`21 February 2026`) but no calendar-invalid matching value. Confidence: High (direct regex analysis; no script or database invocation).
+
+## Medium
+
+- **[Pass 1] The seed is only sequentially idempotent; concurrent applies can insert duplicate natural keys.** Severity: Medium. File: `server/scripts/seed-office-seats.mjs:167-189`. Trigger: two `seedOfficeSeats(..., { apply: true })` calls overlap so both `findOne({ office_category, holder_id })` operations for a seat finish before either `insertOne`. Observable consequence: both calls insert a document for the same purported natural key because the diff adds neither an atomic upsert nor a unique compound index. The only idempotency test calls the function twice sequentially, so the unqualified doc-comment claim “Idempotent by the natural key” and the rerun guidance do not cover this race. Confidence: High (direct control-flow analysis).
+
+## Low
+
+- **[Pass 1] Bare invocation establishes a live connection before rejecting the missing Rene date.** Severity: Low. File: `server/scripts/seed-office-seats.mjs:204-230`. Trigger: invoke the script with zero flags in the documented `server/.env` environment. Observable consequence: argument parsing selects dry-run and a null Rene date, but `main` calls `connectDb()` before `seedOfficeSeats` calls `buildSeatDocs` and throws; this makes no collection query or write, but does contact live Atlas, so the strongest safe failure would validate arguments before connecting and the “dry-run default is what makes that safe” wording omits the avoidable live connection. Confidence: High (direct control-flow analysis; invocation was forbidden and not attempted).
+
+- **[Pass 1] The “second validator” precaution neither creates a second validator nor is needed for these assertions.** Severity: Low. File: `server/tests/oxp-1-office-seats.test.js:193-221`. Trigger: run any N-seats-per-office schema test. Observable consequence: `ajv.compile(officeSeatSchema)` on the same schema object is cached by AJV and can return the same validation function; moreover each assertion evaluates its validation result and `.errors` message before the next validation call, so no later call can overwrite the earlier assertion's message. The tests still prove both individual documents validate, but the comments overstate a simultaneous-validation safeguard and do not themselves prove collection coexistence (the later DB tests do when they run). Confidence: Medium-High (AJV caching semantics plus JavaScript argument evaluation; repository/AJV version not yet opened in this pass).
+
+- **[Pass 1] The stored-document round-trip test only validates a hand-stringified surrogate.** Severity: Low. File: `server/schemas/office_seat.schema.js:86`; `server/tests/oxp-1-office-seats.test.js:101-105,375-379`. Trigger: pass a raw MongoDB document, whose `_id` and non-null `holder_id` are BSON `ObjectId` instances, directly to the schema validator. Observable consequence: both fields fail the schema's string typing; the DB-backed test avoids this by explicitly converting both values with `String(...)`, and the nominal round-trip test constructs `_id` as a string from the outset. That may be the intended JSON boundary, but the diff contains no consumer establishing it, so the test title does not prove a raw stored document round-trips. Confidence: High about the mismatch; Medium about impact because the diff intentionally adds no consumer.
+
+- **[Pass 3a] AC1 is literally unsatisfiable as written because its two named enum sources do not share five values.** Severity: Low. File: `specs/stories/oxp-1-data-lock-office-seat-schema.md:84-93`; `server/schemas/office_seat.schema.js:45-56`. Trigger: audit the implementation against AC1's statement that the same five values are used by both `OFFICE_DATA` and `character.schema.js`. Observable consequence: `OFFICE_DATA` has only four categories and lacks `Administrator`, while the character schema has five; the implementation sensibly follows the character schema and the story's Dev Notes explicitly explain this, but AC1 was not corrected, so literal full-AC conformance cannot be truthfully claimed. Confidence: High (direct source comparison; this is specification debt, not a recommendation to remove Administrator).

Confidence: High (direct control-flow analysis; invocation was forbidden and not attempted).
+
+- **[Pass 1] The “second validator” precaution neither creates a second validator nor is needed for these assertions.** Severity: Low. File: `server/tests/oxp-1-office-seats.test.js:193-221`. Trigger: run any N-seats-per-office schema test. Observable consequence: `ajv.compile(officeSeatSchema)` on the same schema object is cached by AJV and can return the same validation function; moreover each assertion evaluates its validation result and `.errors` message before the next validation call, so no later call can overwrite the earlier assertion's message. The tests still prove both individual documents validate, but the comments overstate a simultaneous-validation safeguard and do not themselves prove collection coexistence (the later DB tests do when they run). Confidence: Medium-High (AJV caching semantics plus JavaScript argument evaluation; repository/AJV version not yet opened in this pass).
+
+- **[Pass 1] The stored-document round-trip test only validates a hand-stringified surrogate.** Severity: Low. File: `server/schemas/office_seat.schema.js:86`; `server/tests/oxp-1-office-seats.test.js:101-105,375-379`. Trigger: pass a raw MongoDB document, whose `_id` and non-null `holder_id` are BSON `ObjectId` instances, directly to the schema validator. Observable consequence: both fields fail the schema's string typing; the DB-backed test avoids this by explicitly converting both values with `String(...)`, and the nominal round-trip test constructs `_id` as a string from the outset. That may be the intended JSON boundary, but the diff contains no consumer establishing it, so the test title does not prove a raw stored document round-trips. Confidence: High about the mismatch; Medium about impact because the diff intentionally adds no consumer.

+- **[Pass 3a] AC1 is literally unsatisfiable as written because its two named enum sources do not share five values.** Severity: Low. File: `specs/stories/oxp-1-data-lock-office-seat-schema.md:84-93`; `server/schemas/office_seat.schema.js:45-56`. Trigger: audit the implementation against AC1's statement that the same five values are used by both `OFFICE_DATA` and `character.schema.js`. Observable consequence: `OFFICE_DATA` has only four categories and lacks `Administrator`, while the character schema has five; the implementation sensibly follows the character schema and the story's Dev Notes explicitly explain this, but AC1 was not corrected, so literal full-AC conformance cannot be truthfully claimed. Confidence: High (direct source comparison; this is specification debt, not a recommendation to remove Administrator).

+## High
+
+- **[Pass 1] The purported ISO-date guard accepts impossible dates and malformed timestamps.** Severity: High. File: `server/schemas/office_seat.schema.js:76`; mirrored in `server/scripts/seed-office-seats.mjs:109`. Trigger: supply Rene's required override as `2026-99-99` (or a syntactically matching timestamp such as `2026-02-21T+++`). The tests cover prose (`21 February 2026`) but no calendar-invalid matching value. Confidence: High (direct regex analysis; no script or database invocation).
+
+## Medium
+

Observable consequence: both calls insert a document for the same purported natural key because the diff adds neither an atomic upsert nor a unique compound index. The only idempotency test calls the function twice sequentially, so the unqualified doc-comment claim “Idempotent by the natural key” and the rerun guidance do not cover this race. Confidence: High (direct control-flow analysis).

+## High
+
+- **[Pass 1] The purported ISO-date guard accepts impossible dates and malformed timestamps.** Severity: High. File: `server/schemas/office_seat.schema.js:76`; mirrored in `server/scripts/seed-office-seats.mjs:109`. Trigger: supply Rene's required override as `2026-99-99` (or a syntactically matching timestamp such as `2026-02-21T+++`). Observable consequence: `buildSeatDocs` accepts the value and an `--apply` run can persist it to the live collection even though downstream date arithmetic can produce `NaN`, exactly the silent bad-XP outcome the guard says it prevents; the schema accepts the same bad value. The tests cover prose (`21 February 2026`) but no calendar-invalid matching value. Confidence: High (direct regex analysis; no script or database invocation).
+
+## Medium
+
+- **[Pass 1] The seed is only sequentially idempotent; concurrent applies can insert duplicate natural keys.** Severity: Medium. File: `server/scripts/seed-office-seats.mjs:167-189`. Trigger: two `seedOfficeSeats(..., { apply: true })` calls overlap so both `findOne({ office_category, holder_id })` operations for a seat finish before either `insertOne`. Observable consequence: both calls insert a document for the same purported natural key because the diff adds neither an atomic upsert nor a unique compound index. The only idempotency test calls the function twice sequentially, so the unqualified doc-comment claim “Idempotent by the natural key” and the rerun guidance do not cover this race. Confidence: High (direct control-flow analysis).

+# Adversarial review — oxp-1
+
+## High
+
+- **[Pass 1] The purported ISO-date guard accepts impossible dates and malformed timestamps.** Severity: High. File: `server/schemas/office_seat.schema.js:76`; mirrored in `server/scripts/seed-office-seats.mjs:109`. Trigger: supply Rene's required override as `2026-99-99` (or a syntactically matching timestamp such as `2026-02-21T+++`). Observable consequence: `buildSeatDocs` accepts the value and an `--apply` run can persist it to the live collection even though downstream date arithmetic can produce `NaN`, exactly the silent bad-XP outcome the guard says it prevents; the schema accepts the same bad value. The tests cover prose (`21 February 2026`) but no calendar-invalid matching value. Confidence: High (direct regex analysis; no script or database invocation).
+
+## Medium
+
+- **[Pass 1] The seed is only sequentially idempotent; concurrent applies can insert duplicate natural keys.** Severity: Medium. File: `server/scripts/seed-office-seats.mjs:167-189`. Trigger: two `seedOfficeSeats(..., { apply: true })` calls overlap so both `findOne({ office_category, holder_id })` operations for a seat finish before either `insertOne`. Observable consequence: both calls insert a document for the same purported natural key because the diff adds neither an atomic upsert nor a unique compound index. The only idempotency test calls the function twice sequentially, so the unqualified doc-comment claim “Idempotent by the natural key” and the rerun guidance do not cover this race. Confidence: High (direct control-flow analysis).
+
+## Low
+
+- **[Pass 1] Bare invocation establishes a live connection before rejecting the missing Rene date.** Severity: Low. File: `server/scripts/seed-office-seats.mjs:204-230`. Trigger: invoke the script with zero flags in the documented `server/.env` environment. Observable consequence: argument parsing selects dry-run and a null Rene date, but `main` calls `connectDb()` before `seedOfficeSeats` calls `buildSeatDocs` and throws; this makes no collection query or write, but does contact live Atlas, so the strongest safe failure would validate arguments before connecting and the “dry-run default is what makes that safe” wording omits the avoidable live connection. Confidence: High (direct control-flow analysis; invocation was forbidden and not attempted).
+
+- **[Pass 1] The “second validator” precaution neither creates a second validator nor is needed for these assertions.** Severity: Low. File: `server/tests/oxp-1-office-seats.test.js:193-221`. Trigger: run any N-seats-per-office schema test. Observable consequence: `ajv.compile(officeSeatSchema)` on the same schema object is cached by AJV and can return the same validation function; moreover each assertion evaluates its validation result and `.errors` message before the next validation call, so no later call can overwrite the earlier assertion's message. The tests still prove both individual documents validate, but the comments overstate a simultaneous-validation safeguard and do not themselves prove collection coexistence (the later DB tests do when they run). Confidence: Medium-High (AJV caching semantics plus JavaScript argument evaluation; repository/AJV version not yet opened in this pass).
+
+- **[Pass 1] The stored-document round-trip test only validates a hand-stringified surrogate.** Severity: Low. File: `server/schemas/office_seat.schema.js:86`; `server/tests/oxp-1-office-seats.test.js:101-105,375-379`. Trigger: pass a raw MongoDB document, whose `_id` and non-null `holder_id` are BSON `ObjectId` instances, directly to the schema validator. Observable consequence: both fields fail the schema's string typing; the DB-backed test avoids this by explicitly converting both values with `String(...)`, and the nominal round-trip test constructs `_id` as a string from the outset. That may be the intended JSON boundary, but the diff contains no consumer establishing it, so the test title does not prove a raw stored document round-trips. Confidence: High about the mismatch; Medium about impact because the diff intentionally adds no consumer.
+
+- **[Pass 3a] AC1 is literally unsatisfiable as written because its two named enum sources do not share five values.** Severity: Low. File: `specs/stories/oxp-1-data-lock-office-seat-schema.md:84-93`; `server/schemas/office_seat.schema.js:45-56`. Trigger: audit the implementation against AC1's statement that the same five values are used by both `OFFICE_DATA` and `character.schema.js`. Observable consequence: `OFFICE_DATA` has only four categories and lacks `Administrator`, while the character schema has five; the implementation sensibly follows the character schema and the story's Dev Notes explicitly explain this, but AC1 was not corrected, so literal full-AC conformance cannot be truthfully claimed. Confidence: High (direct source comparison; this is specification debt, not a recommendation to remove Administrator).
+

This is not mixed storage in the seed path. The Pass 1 Low round-trip limitation remains: the AJV file validates the JSON representation, not a raw stored document, and no consumer yet establishes that boundary.

Sequential reruns meet the AC's expressly permitted existence-check implementation, but the Pass 1 Medium finding qualifies the unbounded “idempotent” claim under concurrent execution. The Pass 1 High finding means a matching but impossible Rene date is not actually rejected.

DB-backed tests, when available, insert same-category documents and call the exported seed function against the injected test collection, checking all seven pairings and sequential reruns. Whether those DB blocks actually ran will be established in Pass 3b's exact gate.

+# Adversarial review — oxp-1
+
+## High
+
+- **[Pass 1] The purported ISO-date guard accepts impossible dates and malformed timestamps.** Severity: High. File: `server/schemas/office_seat.schema.js:76`; mirrored in `server/scripts/seed-office-seats.mjs:109`. Trigger: supply Rene's required override as `2026-99-99` (or a syntactically matching timestamp such as `2026-02-21T+++`). Observable consequence: `buildSeatDocs` accepts the value and an `--apply` run can persist it to the live collection even though downstream date arithmetic can produce `NaN`, exactly the silent bad-XP outcome the guard says it prevents; the schema accepts the same bad value. The tests cover prose (`21 February 2026`) but no calendar-invalid matching value. Confidence: High (direct regex analysis; no script or database invocation).
+
+## Medium
+
+- **[Pass 1] The seed is only sequentially idempotent; concurrent applies can insert duplicate natural keys.** Severity: Medium. File: `server/scripts/seed-office-seats.mjs:167-189`. Trigger: two `seedOfficeSeats(..., { apply: true })` calls overlap so both `findOne({ office_category, holder_id })` operations for a seat finish before either `insertOne`. Observable consequence: both calls insert a document for the same purported natural key because the diff adds neither an atomic upsert nor a unique compound index. The only idempotency test calls the function twice sequentially, so the unqualified doc-comment claim “Idempotent by the natural key” and the rerun guidance do not cover this race. Confidence: High (direct control-flow analysis).
+
+## Low
+
+- **[Pass 1] Bare invocation establishes a live connection before rejecting the missing Rene date.** Severity: Low. File: `server/scripts/seed-office-seats.mjs:204-230`. Trigger: invoke the script with zero flags in the documented `server/.env` environment. Observable consequence: argument parsing selects dry-run and a null Rene date, but `main` calls `connectDb()` before `seedOfficeSeats` calls `buildSeatDocs` and throws; this makes no collection query or write, but does contact live Atlas, so the strongest safe failure would validate arguments before connecting and the “dry-run default is what makes that safe” wording omits the avoidable live connection. Confidence: High (direct control-flow analysis; invocation was forbidden and not attempted).
+
+- **[Pass 1] The “second validator” precaution neither creates a second validator nor is needed for these assertions.** Severity: Low. File: `server/tests/oxp-1-office-seats.test.js:193-221`. Trigger: run any N-seats-per-office schema test. Observable consequence: `ajv.compile(officeSeatSchema)` on the same schema object is cached by AJV and can return the same validation function; moreover each assertion evaluates its validation result and `.errors` message before the next validation call, so no later call can overwrite the earlier assertion's message. The tests still prove both individual documents validate, but the comments overstate a simultaneous-validation safeguard and do not themselves prove collection coexistence (the later DB tests do when they run). Confidence: Medium-High (AJV caching semantics plus JavaScript argument evaluation; repository/AJV version not yet opened in this pass).
+
+- **[Pass 1] The stored-document round-trip test only validates a hand-stringified surrogate.** Severity: Low. File: `server/schemas/office_seat.schema.js:86`; `server/tests/oxp-1-office-seats.test.js:101-105,375-379`. Trigger: pass a raw MongoDB document, whose `_id` and non-null `holder_id` are BSON `ObjectId` instances, directly to the schema validator. Observable consequence: both fields fail the schema's string typing; the DB-backed test avoids this by explicitly converting both values with `String(...)`, and the nominal round-trip test constructs `_id` as a string from the outset. That may be the intended JSON boundary, but the diff contains no consumer establishing it, so the test title does not prove a raw stored document round-trips. Confidence: High about the mismatch; Medium about impact because the diff intentionally adds no consumer.
+
+- **[Pass 3a] AC1 is literally unsatisfiable as written because its two named enum sources do not share five values.** Severity: Low. File: `specs/stories/oxp-1-data-lock-office-seat-schema.md:84-93`; `server/schemas/office_seat.schema.js:45-56`. Trigger: audit the implementation against AC1's statement that the same five values are used by both `OFFICE_DATA` and `character.schema.js`. Observable consequence: `OFFICE_DATA` has only four categories and lacks `Administrator`, while the character schema has five; the implementation sensibly follows the character schema and the story's Dev Notes explicitly explain this, but AC1 was not corrected, so literal full-AC conformance cannot be truthfully claimed. Confidence: High (direct source comparison; this is specification debt, not a recommendation to remove Administrator).

+# Adversarial review — oxp-1
+
+## High
+
+- **[Pass 1] The purported ISO-date guard accepts impossible dates and malformed timestamps.** Severity: High. File: `server/schemas/office_seat.schema.js:76`; mirrored in `server/scripts/seed-office-seats.mjs:109`. Trigger: supply Rene's required override as `2026-99-99` (or a syntactically matching timestamp such as `2026-02-21T+++`). Observable consequence: `buildSeatDocs` accepts the value and an `--apply` run can persist it to the live collection even though downstream date arithmetic can produce `NaN`, exactly the silent bad-XP outcome the guard says it prevents; the schema accepts the same bad value. The tests cover prose (`21 February 2026`) but no calendar-invalid matching value. Confidence: High (direct regex analysis; no script or database invocation).
+
+## Medium
+
+- **[Pass 1] The seed is only sequentially idempotent; concurrent applies can insert duplicate natural keys.** Severity: Medium. File: `server/scripts/seed-office-seats.mjs:167-189`. Trigger: two `seedOfficeSeats(..., { apply: true })` calls overlap so both `findOne({ office_category, holder_id })` operations for a seat finish before either `insertOne`. Observable consequence: both calls insert a document for the same purported natural key because the diff adds neither an atomic upsert nor a unique compound index. The only idempotency test calls the function twice sequentially, so the unqualified doc-comment claim “Idempotent by the natural key” and the rerun guidance do not cover this race. Confidence: High (direct control-flow analysis).
+
+## Low
+
+- **[Pass 1] Bare invocation establishes a live connection before rejecting the missing Rene date.** Severity: Low. File: `server/scripts/seed-office-seats.mjs:204-230`. Trigger: invoke the script with zero flags in the documented `server/.env` environment. Observable consequence: argument parsing selects dry-run and a null Rene date, but `main` calls `connectDb()` before `seedOfficeSeats` calls `buildSeatDocs` and throws; this makes no collection query or write, but does contact live Atlas, so the strongest safe failure would validate arguments before connecting and the “dry-run default is what makes that safe” wording omits the avoidable live connection. Confidence: High (direct control-flow analysis; invocation was forbidden and not attempted).
+
+- **[Pass 1] The “second validator” precaution neither creates a second validator nor is needed for these assertions.** Severity: Low. File: `server/tests/oxp-1-office-seats.test.js:193-221`. Trigger: run any N-seats-per-office schema test. Observable consequence: `ajv.compile(officeSeatSchema)` on the same schema object is cached by AJV and can return the same validation function; moreover each assertion evaluates its validation result and `.errors` message before the next validation call, so no later call can overwrite the earlier assertion's message. The tests still prove both individual documents validate, but the comments overstate a simultaneous-validation safeguard and do not themselves prove collection coexistence (the later DB tests do when they run). Confidence: Medium-High (AJV caching semantics plus JavaScript argument evaluation; repository/AJV version not yet opened in this pass).
+
+- **[Pass 1] The stored-document round-trip test only validates a hand-stringified surrogate.** Severity: Low. File: `server/schemas/office_seat.schema.js:86`; `server/tests/oxp-1-office-seats.test.js:101-105,375-379`. Trigger: pass a raw MongoDB document, whose `_id` and non-null `holder_id` are BSON `ObjectId` instances, directly to the schema validator. Observable consequence: both fields fail the schema's string typing; the DB-backed test avoids this by explicitly converting both values with `String(...)`, and the nominal round-trip test constructs `_id` as a string from the outset. That may be the intended JSON boundary, but the diff contains no consumer establishing it, so the test title does not prove a raw stored document round-trips. Confidence: High about the mismatch; Medium about impact because the diff intentionally adds no consumer.
+
+- **[Pass 3a] AC1 is literally unsatisfiable as written because its two named enum sources do not share five values.** Severity: Low. File: `specs/stories/oxp-1-data-lock-office-seat-schema.md:84-93`; `server/schemas/office_seat.schema.js:45-56`. Trigger: audit the implementation against AC1's statement that the same five values are used by both `OFFICE_DATA` and `character.schema.js`. Observable consequence: `OFFICE_DATA` has only four categories and lacks `Administrator`, while the character schema has five; the implementation sensibly follows the character schema and the story's Dev Notes explicitly explain this, but AC1 was not corrected, so literal full-AC conformance cannot be truthfully claimed. Confidence: High (direct source comparison; this is specification debt, not a recommendation to remove Administrator).

+# Adversarial review — oxp-1
+
+## High
+
+- **[Pass 1] The purported ISO-date guard accepts impossible dates and malformed timestamps.** Severity: High. File: `server/schemas/office_seat.schema.js:76`; mirrored in `server/scripts/seed-office-seats.mjs:109`. Trigger: supply Rene's required override as `2026-99-99` (or a syntactically matching timestamp such as `2026-02-21T+++`). Observable consequence: `buildSeatDocs` accepts the value and an `--apply` run can persist it to the live collection even though downstream date arithmetic can produce `NaN`, exactly the silent bad-XP outcome the guard says it prevents; the schema accepts the same bad value. The tests cover prose (`21 February 2026`) but no calendar-invalid matching value. Confidence: High (direct regex analysis; no script or database invocation).
+
+## Medium
+
+- **[Pass 1] The seed is only sequentially idempotent; concurrent applies can insert duplicate natural keys.** Severity: Medium. File: `server/scripts/seed-office-seats.mjs:167-189`. Trigger: two `seedOfficeSeats(..., { apply: true })` calls overlap so both `findOne({ office_category, holder_id })` operations for a seat finish before either `insertOne`. Observable consequence: both calls insert a document for the same purported natural key because the diff adds neither an atomic upsert nor a unique compound index. The only idempotency test calls the function twice sequentially, so the unqualified doc-comment claim “Idempotent by the natural key” and the rerun guidance do not cover this race. Confidence: High (direct control-flow analysis).
+
+## Low
+
+- **[Pass 1] Bare invocation establishes a live connection before rejecting the missing Rene date.** Severity: Low. File: `server/scripts/seed-office-seats.mjs:204-230`. Trigger: invoke the script with zero flags in the documented `server/.env` environment. Observable consequence: argument parsing selects dry-run and a null Rene date, but `main` calls `connectDb()` before `seedOfficeSeats` calls `buildSeatDocs` and throws; this makes no collection query or write, but does contact live Atlas, so the strongest safe failure would validate arguments before connecting and the “dry-run default is what makes that safe” wording omits the avoidable live connection. Confidence: High (direct control-flow analysis; invocation was forbidden and not attempted).
+
+- **[Pass 1] The “second validator” precaution neither creates a second validator nor is needed for these assertions.** Severity: Low. File: `server/tests/oxp-1-office-seats.test.js:193-221`. Trigger: run any N-seats-per-office schema test. Observable consequence: `ajv.compile(officeSeatSchema)` on the same schema object is cached by AJV and can return the same validation function; moreover each assertion evaluates its validation result and `.errors` message before the next validation call, so no later call can overwrite the earlier assertion's message. The tests still prove both individual documents validate, but the comments overstate a simultaneous-validation safeguard and do not themselves prove collection coexistence (the later DB tests do when they run). Confidence: Medium-High (AJV caching semantics plus JavaScript argument evaluation; repository/AJV version not yet opened in this pass).
+
+- **[Pass 1] The stored-document round-trip test only validates a hand-stringified surrogate.** Severity: Low. File: `server/schemas/office_seat.schema.js:86`; `server/tests/oxp-1-office-seats.test.js:101-105,375-379`. Trigger: pass a raw MongoDB document, whose `_id` and non-null `holder_id` are BSON `ObjectId` instances, directly to the schema validator. Observable consequence: both fields fail the schema's string typing; the DB-backed test avoids this by explicitly converting both values with `String(...)`, and the nominal round-trip test constructs `_id` as a string from the outset. That may be the intended JSON boundary, but the diff contains no consumer establishing it, so the test title does not prove a raw stored document round-trips. Confidence: High about the mismatch; Medium about impact because the diff intentionally adds no consumer.
+
+- **[Pass 3a] AC1 is literally unsatisfiable as written because its two named enum sources do not share five values.** Severity: Low. File: `specs/stories/oxp-1-data-lock-office-seat-schema.md:84-93`; `server/schemas/office_seat.schema.js:45-56`. Trigger: audit the implementation against AC1's statement that the same five values are used by both `OFFICE_DATA` and `character.schema.js`. Observable consequence: `OFFICE_DATA` has only four categories and lacks `Administrator`, while the character schema has five; the implementation sensibly follows the character schema and the story's Dev Notes explicitly explain this, but AC1 was not corrected, so literal full-AC conformance cannot be truthfully claimed. Confidence: High (direct source comparison; this is specification debt, not a recommendation to remove Administrator).
+

+# Adversarial review — oxp-1
+
+## High
+
+- **[Pass 1] The purported ISO-date guard accepts impossible dates and malformed timestamps.** Severity: High. File: `server/schemas/office_seat.schema.js:76`; mirrored in `server/scripts/seed-office-seats.mjs:109`. Trigger: supply Rene's required override as `2026-99-99` (or a syntactically matching timestamp such as `2026-02-21T+++`). Observable consequence: `buildSeatDocs` accepts the value and an `--apply` run can persist it to the live collection even though downstream date arithmetic can produce `NaN`, exactly the silent bad-XP outcome the guard says it prevents; the schema accepts the same bad value. The tests cover prose (`21 February 2026`) but no calendar-invalid matching value. Confidence: High (direct regex analysis; no script or database invocation).
+
+## Medium
+
+- **[Pass 1] The seed is only sequentially idempotent; concurrent applies can insert duplicate natural keys.** Severity: Medium. File: `server/scripts/seed-office-seats.mjs:167-189`. Trigger: two `seedOfficeSeats(..., { apply: true })` calls overlap so both `findOne({ office_category, holder_id })` operations for a seat finish before either `insertOne`. Observable consequence: both calls insert a document for the same purported natural key because the diff adds neither an atomic upsert nor a unique compound index. The only idempotency test calls the function twice sequentially, so the unqualified doc-comment claim “Idempotent by the natural key” and the rerun guidance do not cover this race. Confidence: High (direct control-flow analysis).
+
+## Low
+
+- **[Pass 1] Bare invocation establishes a live connection before rejecting the missing Rene date.** Severity: Low. File: `server/scripts/seed-office-seats.mjs:204-230`. Trigger: invoke the script with zero flags in the documented `server/.env` environment. Observable consequence: argument parsing selects dry-run and a null Rene date, but `main` calls `connectDb()` before `seedOfficeSeats` calls `buildSeatDocs` and throws; this makes no collection query or write, but does contact live Atlas, so the strongest safe failure would validate arguments before connecting and the “dry-run default is what makes that safe” wording omits the avoidable live connection. Confidence: High (direct control-flow analysis; invocation was forbidden and not attempted).
+
+- **[Pass 1] The “second validator” precaution neither creates a second validator nor is needed for these assertions.** Severity: Low. File: `server/tests/oxp-1-office-seats.test.js:193-221`. Trigger: run any N-seats-per-office schema test. Observable consequence: `ajv.compile(officeSeatSchema)` on the same schema object is cached by AJV and can return the same validation function; moreover each assertion evaluates its validation result and `.errors` message before the next validation call, so no later call can overwrite the earlier assertion's message. The tests still prove both individual documents validate, but the comments overstate a simultaneous-validation safeguard and do not themselves prove collection coexistence (the later DB tests do when they run). Confidence: Medium-High (AJV caching semantics plus JavaScript argument evaluation; repository/AJV version not yet opened in this pass).
+
+- **[Pass 1] The stored-document round-trip test only validates a hand-stringified surrogate.** Severity: Low. File: `server/schemas/office_seat.schema.js:86`; `server/tests/oxp-1-office-seats.test.js:101-105,375-379`. Trigger: pass a raw MongoDB document, whose `_id` and non-null `holder_id` are BSON `ObjectId` instances, directly to the schema validator. Observable consequence: both fields fail the schema's string typing; the DB-backed test avoids this by explicitly converting both values with `String(...)`, and the nominal round-trip test constructs `_id` as a string from the outset. That may be the intended JSON boundary, but the diff contains no consumer establishing it, so the test title does not prove a raw stored document round-trips. Confidence: High about the mismatch; Medium about impact because the diff intentionally adds no consumer.
+
+- **[Pass 3a] AC1 is literally unsatisfiable as written because its two named enum sources do not share five values.** Severity: Low. File: `specs/stories/oxp-1-data-lock-office-seat-schema.md:84-93`; `server/schemas/office_seat.schema.js:45-56`. Trigger: audit the implementation against AC1's statement that the same five values are used by both `OFFICE_DATA` and `character.schema.js`. Observable consequence: `OFFICE_DATA` has only four categories and lacks `Administrator`, while the character schema has five; the implementation sensibly follows the character schema and the story's Dev Notes explicitly explain this, but AC1 was not corrected, so literal full-AC conformance cannot be truthfully claimed. Confidence: High (direct source comparison; this is specification debt, not a recommendation to remove Administrator).

+# Adversarial review — oxp-1
+
+## High
+
+- **[Pass 1] The purported ISO-date guard accepts impossible dates and malformed timestamps.** Severity: High. File: `server/schemas/office_seat.schema.js:76`; mirrored in `server/scripts/seed-office-seats.mjs:109`. Trigger: supply Rene's required override as `2026-99-99` (or a syntactically matching timestamp such as `2026-02-21T+++`). Observable consequence: `buildSeatDocs` accepts the value and an `--apply` run can persist it to the live collection even though downstream date arithmetic can produce `NaN`, exactly the silent bad-XP outcome the guard says it prevents; the schema accepts the same bad value. The tests cover prose (`21 February 2026`) but no calendar-invalid matching value. Confidence: High (direct regex analysis; no script or database invocation).
+
+## Medium
+
+- **[Pass 1] The seed is only sequentially idempotent; concurrent applies can insert duplicate natural keys.** Severity: Medium. File: `server/scripts/seed-office-seats.mjs:167-189`. Trigger: two `seedOfficeSeats(..., { apply: true })` calls overlap so both `findOne({ office_category, holder_id })` operations for a seat finish before either `insertOne`. Observable consequence: both calls insert a document for the same purported natural key because the diff adds neither an atomic upsert nor a unique compound index. The only idempotency test calls the function twice sequentially, so the unqualified doc-comment claim “Idempotent by the natural key” and the rerun guidance do not cover this race. Confidence: High (direct control-flow analysis).
+
+## Low
+
+- **[Pass 1] Bare invocation establishes a live connection before rejecting the missing Rene date.** Severity: Low. File: `server/scripts/seed-office-seats.mjs:204-230`. Trigger: invoke the script with zero flags in the documented `server/.env` environment. Observable consequence: argument parsing selects dry-run and a null Rene date, but `main` calls `connectDb()` before `seedOfficeSeats` calls `buildSeatDocs` and throws; this makes no collection query or write, but does contact live Atlas, so the strongest safe failure would validate arguments before connecting and the “dry-run default is what makes that safe” wording omits the avoidable live connection. Confidence: High (direct control-flow analysis; invocation was forbidden and not attempted).
+
+- **[Pass 1] The “second validator” precaution neither creates a second validator nor is needed for these assertions.** Severity: Low. File: `server/tests/oxp-1-office-seats.test.js:193-221`. Trigger: run any N-seats-per-office schema test. Observable consequence: `ajv.compile(officeSeatSchema)` on the same schema object is cached by AJV and can return the same validation function; moreover each assertion evaluates its validation result and `.errors` message before the next validation call, so no later call can overwrite the earlier assertion's message. The tests still prove both individual documents validate, but the comments overstate a simultaneous-validation safeguard and do not themselves prove collection coexistence (the later DB tests do when they run). Confidence: Medium-High (AJV caching semantics plus JavaScript argument evaluation; repository/AJV version not yet opened in this pass).
+
+- **[Pass 1] The stored-document round-trip test only validates a hand-stringified surrogate.** Severity: Low. File: `server/schemas/office_seat.schema.js:86`; `server/tests/oxp-1-office-seats.test.js:101-105,375-379`. Trigger: pass a raw MongoDB document, whose `_id` and non-null `holder_id` are BSON `ObjectId` instances, directly to the schema validator. Observable consequence: both fields fail the schema's string typing; the DB-backed test avoids this by explicitly converting both values with `String(...)`, and the nominal round-trip test constructs `_id` as a string from the outset. That may be the intended JSON boundary, but the diff contains no consumer establishing it, so the test title does not prove a raw stored document round-trips. Confidence: High about the mismatch; Medium about impact because the diff intentionally adds no consumer.

Trigger: audit the implementation against AC1's statement that the same five values are used by both `OFFICE_DATA` and `character.schema.js`. Observable consequence: `buildSeatDocs` accepts the value and an `--apply` run can persist it to the live collection even though downstream date arithmetic can produce `NaN`, exactly the silent bad-XP outcome the guard says it prevents; the schema accepts the same bad value. The tests cover prose (`21 February 2026`) but no calendar-invalid matching value. Confidence: High (direct regex analysis; no script or database invocation).
+
+## Medium
+
+- **[Pass 1] The seed is only sequentially idempotent; concurrent applies can insert duplicate natural keys.** Severity: Medium. File: `server/scripts/seed-office-seats.mjs:167-189`. Trigger: two `seedOfficeSeats(..., { apply: true })` calls overlap so both `findOne({ office_category, holder_id })` operations for a seat finish before either `insertOne`. Observable consequence: both calls insert a document for the same purported natural key because the diff adds neither an atomic upsert nor a unique compound index. The only idempotency test calls the function twice sequentially, so the unqualified doc-comment claim “Idempotent by the natural key” and the rerun guidance do not cover this race. Confidence: High (direct control-flow analysis).
+
+## Low
+
+- **[Pass 1] Bare invocation establishes a live connection before rejecting the missing Rene date.** Severity: Low. File: `server/scripts/seed-office-seats.mjs:204-230`. Trigger: invoke the script with zero flags in the documented `server/.env` environment. Observable consequence: argument parsing selects dry-run and a null Rene date, but `main` calls `connectDb()` before `seedOfficeSeats` calls `buildSeatDocs` and throws; this makes no collection query or write, but does contact live Atlas, so the strongest safe failure would validate arguments before connecting and the “dry-run default is what makes that safe” wording omits the avoidable live connection. Confidence: High (direct control-flow analysis; invocation was forbidden and not attempted).
+
+- **[Pass 1] The “second validator” precaution neither creates a second validator nor is needed for these assertions.** Severity: Low. File: `server/tests/oxp-1-office-seats.test.js:193-221`. Trigger: run any N-seats-per-office schema test. Observable consequence: `ajv.compile(officeSeatSchema)` on the same schema object is cached by AJV and can return the same validation function; moreover each assertion evaluates its validation result and `.errors` message before the next validation call, so no later call can overwrite the earlier assertion's message. The tests still prove both individual documents validate, but the comments overstate a simultaneous-validation safeguard and do not themselves prove collection coexistence (the later DB tests do when they run). Confidence: Medium-High (AJV caching semantics plus JavaScript argument evaluation; repository/AJV version not yet opened in this pass).
+
+- **[Pass 1] The stored-document round-trip test only validates a hand-stringified surrogate.** Severity: Low. File: `server/schemas/office_seat.schema.js:86`; `server/tests/oxp-1-office-seats.test.js:101-105,375-379`. Trigger: pass a raw MongoDB document, whose `_id` and non-null `holder_id` are BSON `ObjectId` instances, directly to the schema validator. Observable consequence: both fields fail the schema's string typing; the DB-backed test avoids this by explicitly converting both values with `String(...)`, and the nominal round-trip test constructs `_id` as a string from the outset. That may be the intended JSON boundary, but the diff contains no consumer establishing it, so the test title does not prove a raw stored document round-trips. Confidence: High about the mismatch; Medium about impact because the diff intentionally adds no consumer.
+
+- **[Pass 3a] AC1 is literally unsatisfiable as written because its two named enum sources do not share five values.** Severity: Low. File: `specs/stories/oxp-1-data-lock-office-seat-schema.md:84-93`; `server/schemas/office_seat.schema.js:45-56`. Trigger: audit the implementation against AC1's statement that the same five values are used by both `OFFICE_DATA` and `character.schema.js`. Observable consequence: `OFFICE_DATA` has only four categories and lacks `Administrator`, while the character schema has five; the implementation sensibly follows the character schema and the story's Dev Notes explicitly explain this, but AC1 was not corrected, so literal full-AC conformance cannot be truthfully claimed. Confidence: High (direct source comparison; this is specification debt, not a recommendation to remove Administrator).

+# Adversarial review — oxp-1
+
+## High
+
+- **[Pass 1] The purported ISO-date guard accepts impossible dates and malformed timestamps.** Severity: High. File: `server/schemas/office_seat.schema.js:76`; mirrored in `server/scripts/seed-office-seats.mjs:109`. Trigger: supply Rene's required override as `2026-99-99` (or a syntactically matching timestamp such as `2026-02-21T+++`). Observable consequence: `buildSeatDocs` accepts the value and an `--apply` run can persist it to the live collection even though downstream date arithmetic can produce `NaN`, exactly the silent bad-XP outcome the guard says it prevents; the schema accepts the same bad value. The tests cover prose (`21 February 2026`) but no calendar-invalid matching value. Confidence: High (direct regex analysis; no script or database invocation).
+
+## Medium
+
+- **[Pass 1] The seed is only sequentially idempotent; concurrent applies can insert duplicate natural keys.** Severity: Medium. File: `server/scripts/seed-office-seats.mjs:167-189`. Trigger: two `seedOfficeSeats(..., { apply: true })` calls overlap so both `findOne({ office_category, holder_id })` operations for a seat finish before either `insertOne`. Observable consequence: both calls insert a document for the same purported natural key because the diff adds neither an atomic upsert nor a unique compound index. The only idempotency test calls the function twice sequentially, so the unqualified doc-comment claim “Idempotent by the natural key” and the rerun guidance do not cover this race. Confidence: High (direct control-flow analysis).
+
+## Low
+
+- **[Pass 1] Bare invocation establishes a live connection before rejecting the missing Rene date.** Severity: Low. File: `server/scripts/seed-office-seats.mjs:204-230`. Trigger: invoke the script with zero flags in the documented `server/.env` environment. Observable consequence: argument parsing selects dry-run and a null Rene date, but `main` calls `connectDb()` before `seedOfficeSeats` calls `buildSeatDocs` and throws; this makes no collection query or write, but does contact live Atlas, so the strongest safe failure would validate arguments before connecting and the “dry-run default is what makes that safe” wording omits the avoidable live connection. Confidence: High (direct control-flow analysis; invocation was forbidden and not attempted).
+
+- **[Pass 1] The “second validator” precaution neither creates a second validator nor is needed for these assertions.** Severity: Low. File: `server/tests/oxp-1-office-seats.test.js:193-221`. Trigger: run any N-seats-per-office schema test. Observable consequence: `ajv.compile(officeSeatSchema)` on the same schema object is cached by AJV and can return the same validation function; moreover each assertion evaluates its validation result and `.errors` message before the next validation call, so no later call can overwrite the earlier assertion's message. The tests still prove both individual documents validate, but the comments overstate a simultaneous-validation safeguard and do not themselves prove collection coexistence (the later DB tests do when they run). Confidence: Medium-High (AJV caching semantics plus JavaScript argument evaluation; repository/AJV version not yet opened in this pass).
+
+- **[Pass 1] The stored-document round-trip test only validates a hand-stringified surrogate.** Severity: Low. File: `server/schemas/office_seat.schema.js:86`; `server/tests/oxp-1-office-seats.test.js:101-105,375-379`. Trigger: pass a raw MongoDB document, whose `_id` and non-null `holder_id` are BSON `ObjectId` instances, directly to the schema validator. Observable consequence: both fields fail the schema's string typing; the DB-backed test avoids this by explicitly converting both values with `String(...)`, and the nominal round-trip test constructs `_id` as a string from the outset. That may be the intended JSON boundary, but the diff contains no consumer establishing it, so the test title does not prove a raw stored document round-trips. Confidence: High about the mismatch; Medium about impact because the diff intentionally adds no consumer.
+
+- **[Pass 3a] AC1 is literally unsatisfiable as written because its two named enum sources do not share five values.** Severity: Low. File: `specs/stories/oxp-1-data-lock-office-seat-schema.md:84-93`; `server/schemas/office_seat.schema.js:45-56`. Trigger: audit the implementation against AC1's statement that the same five values are used by both `OFFICE_DATA` and `character.schema.js`. Observable consequence: `OFFICE_DATA` has only four categories and lacks `Administrator`, while the character schema has five; the implementation sensibly follows the character schema and the story's Dev Notes explicitly explain this, but AC1 was not corrected, so literal full-AC conformance cannot be truthfully claimed. Confidence: High (direct source comparison; this is specification debt, not a recommendation to remove Administrator).

+# Adversarial review — oxp-1
+
+## High
+
+- **[Pass 1] The purported ISO-date guard accepts impossible dates and malformed timestamps.** Severity: High. File: `server/schemas/office_seat.schema.js:76`; mirrored in `server/scripts/seed-office-seats.mjs:109`. Trigger: supply Rene's required override as `2026-99-99` (or a syntactically matching timestamp such as `2026-02-21T+++`). Observable consequence: `buildSeatDocs` accepts the value and an `--apply` run can persist it to the live collection even though downstream date arithmetic can produce `NaN`, exactly the silent bad-XP outcome the guard says it prevents; the schema accepts the same bad value. The tests cover prose (`21 February 2026`) but no calendar-invalid matching value. Confidence: High (direct regex analysis; no script or database invocation).
+
+## Medium
+
+- **[Pass 1] The seed is only sequentially idempotent; concurrent applies can insert duplicate natural keys.** Severity: Medium. File: `server/scripts/seed-office-seats.mjs:167-189`. Trigger: two `seedOfficeSeats(..., { apply: true })` calls overlap so both `findOne({ office_category, holder_id })` operations for a seat finish before either `insertOne`. Observable consequence: both calls insert a document for the same purported natural key because the diff adds neither an atomic upsert nor a unique compound index. The only idempotency test calls the function twice sequentially, so the unqualified doc-comment claim “Idempotent by the natural key” and the rerun guidance do not cover this race. Confidence: High (direct control-flow analysis).
+
+## Low
+
+- **[Pass 1] Bare invocation establishes a live connection before rejecting the missing Rene date.** Severity: Low. File: `server/scripts/seed-office-seats.mjs:204-230`. Trigger: invoke the script with zero flags in the documented `server/.env` environment. Observable consequence: argument parsing selects dry-run and a null Rene date, but `main` calls `connectDb()` before `seedOfficeSeats` calls `buildSeatDocs` and throws; this makes no collection query or write, but does contact live Atlas, so the strongest safe failure would validate arguments before connecting and the “dry-run default is what makes that safe” wording omits the avoidable live connection. Confidence: High (direct control-flow analysis; invocation was forbidden and not attempted).
+
+- **[Pass 1] The “second validator” precaution neither creates a second validator nor is needed for these assertions.** Severity: Low. File: `server/tests/oxp-1-office-seats.test.js:193-221`. Trigger: run any N-seats-per-office schema test. Observable consequence: `ajv.compile(officeSeatSchema)` on the same schema object is cached by AJV and can return the same validation function; moreover each assertion evaluates its validation result and `.errors` message before the next validation call, so no later call can overwrite the earlier assertion's message. The tests still prove both individual documents validate, but the comments overstate a simultaneous-validation safeguard and do not themselves prove collection coexistence (the later DB tests do when they run). Confidence: Medium-High (AJV caching semantics plus JavaScript argument evaluation; repository/AJV version not yet opened in this pass).
+
+- **[Pass 1] The stored-document round-trip test only validates a hand-stringified surrogate.** Severity: Low. File: `server/schemas/office_seat.schema.js:86`; `server/tests/oxp-1-office-seats.test.js:101-105,375-379`. Trigger: pass a raw MongoDB document, whose `_id` and non-null `holder_id` are BSON `ObjectId` instances, directly to the schema validator. Observable consequence: both fields fail the schema's string typing; the DB-backed test avoids this by explicitly converting both values with `String(...)`, and the nominal round-trip test constructs `_id` as a string from the outset. That may be the intended JSON boundary, but the diff contains no consumer establishing it, so the test title does not prove a raw stored document round-trips. Confidence: High about the mismatch; Medium about impact because the diff intentionally adds no consumer.
+
+- **[Pass 3a] AC1 is literally unsatisfiable as written because its two named enum sources do not share five values.** Severity: Low. File: `specs/stories/oxp-1-data-lock-office-seat-schema.md:84-93`; `server/schemas/office_seat.schema.js:45-56`. Trigger: audit the implementation against AC1's statement that the same five values are used by both `OFFICE_DATA` and `character.schema.js`. Observable consequence: `OFFICE_DATA` has only four categories and lacks `Administrator`, while the character schema has five; the implementation sensibly follows the character schema and the story's Dev Notes explicitly explain this, but AC1 was not corrected, so literal full-AC conformance cannot be truthfully claimed. Confidence: High (direct source comparison; this is specification debt, not a recommendation to remove Administrator).
+
+- **[Pass 3b] The Dev Agent Record overstates the N-seat test evidence.** Severity: Low. File: `specs/stories/oxp-1-data-lock-office-seat-schema.md:357-365`; `server/tests/oxp-1-office-seats.test.js:189-226,350-392`. Trigger: compare the completion-note prose to the four schema tests and three DB tests. Observable consequence: only three schema tests validate pairs; the fourth merely searches the schema text for selected cap keywords. The purported “second” AJV validator is the same cached function, and the assertions are sequential. Of the three DB coexistence tests, only the two Primogen documents are stringified and schema-validated; the Socialite and vacant-seat documents are not, so “every stored document still validates” is not established across that block. Real Mongo coexistence is still proved when DB access is available, but the record describes broader evidence than exists. Confidence: High (direct test-body comparison and confirmed AJV function identity).
+
+- **[Pass 3b] The recorded green gate and two DB-dependent mutation counts are not reproducible in the current environment.** Severity: Low. File: `specs/stories/oxp-1-data-lock-office-seat-schema.md:305-321,343-355`. Trigger: run the exact six-file gate and then the four recorded mutations one at a time. Observable consequence: the exact gate exited 1 with 62 passed and 50 skipped (112 total), two failed suites, three passed files, and one skipped file because Atlas connectivity failed with `EACCES`. The holder-pattern mutation reproduced exactly 3 failures and the category-enum mutation exactly 2. Disabling `if (existing)` produced 32 pass/9 skip because both claimed failures are DB-backed; softening the Rene default produced 1 pure failure while its second claimed DB failure skipped. These results do not prove the historical claims false, but the 112/112 zero-skip claim and the two DB-dependent exact counts are unverifiable-as-stated in this review session and must not be reported as current gate results. Confidence: High about current results; historical run unverifiable.

+- **[Pass 3b] The historical “live database was never connected” claim is not independently verifiable from repository state.** Severity: Low. File: `specs/stories/oxp-1-data-lock-office-seat-schema.md:325-330`. Trigger: audit a claim about actions in the prior authoring session without an immutable connection/audit log in the supplied artifacts. Observable consequence: source structure and the test guard support the account, and nothing found contradicts it, but this review can only attest to its own commands; it cannot prove a previous process never contacted `tm_suite`. Confidence: High that the claim is epistemically unverifiable here; no evidence it is false.
